sentences.zh: 序

translations.literal: Preface.
translations.idiomatic: Prefatory essay to the treatise.

sentences.zh: 夫帝王者，配德天地，葉契陰陽，發號施令，動關幽顯，休咎之徵，隨感而作，故《書》曰：「惠迪吉，從逆凶，惟影響。

translations.literal: Now the ruler who is termed emperor-king matches virtue with Heaven and Earth, accords with Yin and Yang, issues commands and promulgates orders, and his acts bear upon what is hidden and what is manifest alike; the omens of blessing and calamity arise as responses to stimuli; therefore the Documents says: "Following the right course brings good fortune; following the rebellious course brings misfortune—as surely as shadow and echo."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor-king aligns his virtue with Heaven and Earth and harmonizes Yin and Yang; every decree he issues touches both the unseen and the seen, and portents of fortune or disaster arise as immediate echoes of conduct. The Book of Documents therefore warns that those who walk the true path are blessed, while those who defy it invite calamity—swiftly and inevitably, like shadow answering form or echo answering sound.

sentences.zh: 」昔伏羲氏繼天而王，受《河圖》，則而畫之，八卦是也。

translations.literal: " In antiquity Fuxi succeeded Heaven as king; he received the River Chart, took it as model and delineated it—the Eight Trigrams are this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in high antiquity Fuxi claimed the kingship as heir to Heaven; granted the Yellow River Chart, he patterned himself on it and drew forth the Eight Trigrams.

sentences.zh: 禹治洪水，賜《洛書》，法而陳之，《洪範》是也。

translations.literal: Yu controlled the floodwaters; he was granted the Luo Writing, took its pattern and displayed it—the Hong Fan is this.
translations.idiomatic: Yu tamed the floods and received the writing from the Luo; he codified its principles and set them forth—that text became the "Great Plan" chapter of the Documents.

sentences.zh: 聖人行其道，寶其真，自天祐之，吉無不利。

translations.literal: The sage practices its Way and treasures its truth; Heaven itself blesses him, and there is no good fortune that does not attend him.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage walks that Way and guards its truth, Heaven lends its aid, and every outcome proves auspicious.

sentences.zh: 三五已降，各有司存。

translations.literal: From the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors downward, each age had its appointed keeper.
translations.idiomatic: After the era of the legendary Three and Five, each period entrusted these teachings to its own guardians.

sentences.zh: 爰及殷之箕子，在父師之位，典斯大範。

translations.literal: Thus extending to Jizi of Yin, who stood in the rank of Father-instructor and presided over this great norm.
translations.idiomatic: Among them was Jizi under Yin, Father-instructor to the throne, custodian of this overarching paradigm.

sentences.zh: 周既克殷，以箕子歸，武王虛己而問焉。

translations.literal: When Zhou had conquered Yin, it brought Jizi back with it; King Wu emptied himself of self-importance and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhou had overthrown Yin, Jizi returned at its summons; King Wu bowed his pride and sought his counsel.

sentences.zh: 箕子對以禹所得《雒書》，授之以垂訓。

translations.literal: Jizi replied with what Yu had obtained—the Luo Writing—and imparted it for enduring instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Jizi answered with the Luo River scripture Yu had once received, transmitting its lesson as a lasting moral charter.

sentences.zh: 然則《河圖》、《雒書》相為經緯，八卦、九章更為表裏。

translations.literal: Accordingly the River Chart and the Luo Writing are warp and woof to each other; the Eight Trigrams and the Nine Sections are outer and inner to each other.
translations.idiomatic: The River Chart and Luo Writing thus interlock like warp and weft; the Eight Trigrams and the nine divisions of the Great Plan overlay one another as shell and core.

sentences.zh: 殷道絕，文王演《周易》；

translations.literal: When the way of Yin was cut off, King Wen elaborated the Zhou Changes;
translations.idiomatic: When Yin’s mandate failed, King Wen unfolded the Zhou yi.

sentences.zh: 周道弊，孔子述《春秋》。

translations.literal: when the way of Zhou decayed, Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou’s authority frayed, Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 奉乾坤之陰陽，郊洪範之休咎，天人之道粲然著矣。

translations.literal: Upholding the Yin and Yang of Qian and Kun, attaching the blessing and calamity of the Hong Fan at the suburban sacrifice—the way of Heaven and man is thereby radiant and plain.
translations.idiomatic: They upheld Qian and Kun’s interplay of Yin and Yang and brought the Great Plan’s calculus of blessing and blame into the suburban rites—so the correspondence between Heaven and humanity stands forth in unmistakable clarity.

sentences.zh: 漢興，承秦滅學之後，文帝時，虙生創紀《大傳》，其言五行庶徵備矣。

translations.literal: When Han arose, inheriting after Qin's destruction of learning, in Emperor Wen's time Fu Sheng founded the chronicle of the Greater Commentary, and his discourse on the Five Elements and multifarious signs was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Han emerged from the ruins of Qin's assault on scholarship; during Emperor Wen's reign Fu Sheng framed the chronology of the Greater Commentary, and his chapter on the Five Elements with their diverse portents was already exhaustive.

sentences.zh: 後景武之際，董仲舒治《公羊春秋》，始推陰陽，為儒者之宗。

translations.literal: Later, at the time of Emperors Jing and Wu, Dong Zhongshu studied the Gongyang Spring and Autumn; he first extended Yin and Yang and became the patriarch of the Ru scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Jing and Wu, Dong Zhongshu took up the Gongyang Annals and pioneered correlating Yin and Yang with historical judgment, earning recognition as the fountainhead of Han Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 宣元之間，劉向治《谷梁春秋》，數其禍福，傳以《洪範》，與仲舒多所不同。

translations.literal: Between Emperors Xuan and Yuan, Liu Xiang studied the Guliang Spring and Autumn, reckoned its calamities and blessings, transmitted it with the Hong Fan, and differed from Zhongshu in many respects.
translations.idiomatic: Across the Xuan–Yuan reigns Liu Xiang worked through the Guliang commentary, tallying fortune and disaster line by line and pairing his conclusions with the Great Plan—often diverging sharply from Dong Zhongshu.

sentences.zh: 至向子歆治《左氏傳》，其言《春秋》及五行，又甚乖異。

translations.literal: When it came to Liu Xiang's son Xin studying the Zuo Commentary, his statements on the Spring and Autumn and on the Five Elements were again greatly contrary and divergent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin then approached the Zuo Tradition and produced yet another reading of the Annals and the Five Elements, wildly at odds with both earlier paradigms.

sentences.zh: 班固據《大傳》，采仲舒、劉向、劉歆著《五行志》，而傳載眭孟、夏侯勝、京房、谷永、李尋之徒所陳行事，訖于王莽，博通祥變，以傳《春秋》。

translations.literal: Ban Gu relied on the Greater Commentary, gathered Dong Zhongshu, Liu Xiang, and Liu Xin and composed the Treatise on the Five Elements, and in transmitting recorded the deeds related by Sui Meng, Xiahou Sheng, Jing Fang, Gu Yong, Li Xun and their like, down to Wang Mang, broadly comprehending auspicious anomalies to transmit the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu anchored his narrative in the Greater Commentary and synthesized Dong Zhongshu with father and son Liu into the Han Treatise on the Five Elements; its records preserve testimony from Sui Meng, Xiahou Sheng, Jing Fang, Gu Yong, Li Xun, and others down through Wang Mang—an encyclopedic survey of prodigies intended to extend the moral algebra of the Annals.

sentences.zh: 綜而為言，凡有三術。

translations.literal: Taken together and stated in summary, there are in all three methods.
translations.idiomatic: Reduced to essentials, the exegetical tradition offers three recurring interpretive moves.

sentences.zh: 其一曰，君治以道，臣輔克忠，萬物咸遂其性，則和氣應，休徵效，國以安。

translations.literal: The first says: if the lord governs by the Way and ministers assist with full loyalty, the myriad things all realize their natures, then harmonious qi responds, auspicious signs appear, and the state is thereby secure.
translations.idiomatic: First: when the ruler upholds the Way and ministers serve with perfect fidelity, creation fulfills its innate tendencies, harmonious energies gather, felicitous omens multiply, and the realm stays at peace.

sentences.zh: 二曰，君違其道，小人在位，眾庶失常，則乖氣應，咎徵效，國以亡。

translations.literal: Second says: if the lord violates its Way, petty men hold office, and the masses lose their constants, then perverse qi responds, calamitous signs appear, and the state thereby perishes.
translations.idiomatic: Second: when the throne abandons the Way, petty men crowd the councils, and common folk lose their moral bearings, disruptive energies answer, baleful omens cluster, and the dynasty slides toward extinction.

sentences.zh: 三曰，人君大臣見災異，退而自省，責躬修德，共禦補過，則消禍而福至。

translations.literal: Third says: when lord and great ministers see disasters and anomalies, they withdraw and examine themselves, blame their persons and cultivate virtue, jointly ward off and remedy faults, then calamity is dispelled and blessing arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Third: when sovereign and senior ministers heed Heaven's warnings, retire into self-scrutiny, discipline their persons, and cooperate to redress misrule, catastrophe may yet be averted and blessing renewed.

sentences.zh: 此其大略也。

translations.literal: This is its general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the broad scheme.

sentences.zh: 輒舉斯例，錯綜時變，婉而成章，有足觀者。

translations.literal: Whenever one adduces this pattern, interweaving the changes of the times, it forms elegant compositions—there is enough worth observing.
translations.idiomatic: Deploy these templates against shifting historical circumstances and they braid into narratives subtle yet coherent—eminently worth studying.

sentences.zh: 及司馬彪纂光武之後以究漢事，災眚之說不越前規。

translations.literal: When Sima Biao compiled after Guangwu to investigate Han affairs, the discourse on disasters and calamities did not overstep prior norms.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Biao continued the Later Han record from Guangwu onward, his handling of calamities and ill omens still respected the older analytical frame.

sentences.zh: 今采黃初以降言祥異者，著於此篇。

translations.literal: Now I gather from Huangchu downward those who spoke of auspicious anomalies and record them in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Here I compile every noteworthy prodigy reported from the Huangchu era forward and set them down in this treatise.

sentences.zh: 五行

translations.literal: The Five Elements.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise: The Five Elements, also called the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 《經》曰：「五行：一曰水，二曰火，三曰木，四曰金，五曰土。

translations.literal: The Classic says: "The Five Elements: first they are called water, second fire, third wood, fourth metal, fifth earth.
translations.idiomatic: The canon declares: "Among the Five Phases, reckoning runs water first, fire second, wood third, metal fourth, earth fifth.

sentences.zh: 水曰潤下，火曰炎上，木曰曲直，金曰從革，土爰稼穡。」

translations.literal: Water is called moistening downward, fire is called blazing upward, wood is called bending and straightening, metal is called obeying and transforming, earth is called sowing and reaping."
translations.idiomatic: Water's nature is to soak downward; fire's is to flame upward; wood bends and straightens; metal yields and can be recast; earth receives the seed and ripens the crop."

translations.literal: Graphical equals sign marking column alignment in the source table.
translations.idiomatic: Column spacer preserved from the tabular exemplar.

sentences.zh: 木

translations.literal: Wood.
translations.idiomatic: Wood — the eastern phase.

sentences.zh: =《傳》曰：「田獵不宿，飲食不享，出入不節，奪農時及有奸謀，則木不曲直。」

translations.literal: =The Commentary says: "If hunting does not lodge overnight, eating and drinking are not offered in sacrifice, coming and going lack restraint, agricultural seasons are seized, and there are treacherous plots, then wood does not bend and straighten."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary continues: "When hunts roll on without pause, feasts ignore sacrificial propriety, movement ignores measure, corvées steal the farming calendar, and treachery festers, wood forfeits its office of bending and straightening."

sentences.zh: 說曰：木，東方也。

translations.literal: The explanation says: Wood is the east.
translations.idiomatic: Exposition: Wood correlates with the east.

sentences.zh: 于《易》，地上之木為《觀》。

translations.literal: In the Changes, wood upon the earth constitutes the hexagram Guan, "Viewing."
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhou yi wood springing from soil forms the hexagram Guan, the figure entitled "Viewing."

sentences.zh: 于王事，威儀容貌亦可觀者也。

translations.literal: In royal affairs, awe-inspiring bearing and appearance are also things that may be observed.
translations.idiomatic: In matters of state, dignified bearing and department are meant to be exemplary—to edify all who behold them.

sentences.zh: 故行步有佩玉之度，登車有和鸞之節，三驅之制，飲食有享獻之禮；

translations.literal: Therefore in walking there is the measure of jade pendants; in mounting a carriage there is the harmony of the carriage-bells; there is the regulation of the three hunts; in eating and drinking there is the rite of offering and presenting;
translations.idiomatic: Hence gait keeps time with belt-jades; chariot teams answer with tuned bells; the royal hunt limits itself to the thrice-driven quarry; at table every cup and dish observes the rhythms of offering and sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 出入有名，使人以時，務在勸農桑，謀在安百姓，如此，則木得其性矣。

translations.literal: coming and going have proper names; sending forth others observes the seasons; the endeavor lies in encouraging farming and sericulture, the planning lies in securing the hundred clans—thus wood obtains its nature.
translations.idiomatic: every mission travels under clear warrant; labor is summoned only in season with agriculture and sericulture promoted and the people's welfare the governing aim—only then does wood realize its true character.

sentences.zh: 若乃田獵馳騁，不反宮室；

translations.literal: If then hunting gallops and races and does not return to palace chambers;
translations.idiomatic: When the chase becomes endless roaming that never returns courtward,

sentences.zh: 飲食沈湎，不顧法度；

translations.literal: eating and drinking sink and drown without regard to statutes and measures;
translations.idiomatic: when feasting sinks into dissipation heedless of statute,

sentences.zh: 妄興徭役，以奪農時；

translations.literal: rashly raising corvée labor to seize the farming seasons;
translations.idiomatic: when arbitrary corvées tear farmers from their proper seasons,

sentences.zh: 作為奸詐，以傷人財，則木失其性矣。

translations.literal: acting treacherously and deceitfully to harm people's wealth—then wood loses its nature.
translations.idiomatic: and deceit drains the common people's substance—wood abandons its appointed nature.

sentences.zh: 蓋工匠之為輪矢者多傷敗，及木為變怪，是為不曲直。

translations.literal: Generally cartwrights who make wheels and arrows mostly suffer injury and ruin, and when wood becomes strange anomalies, this is not bending and straightening.
translations.idiomatic: Wheelwrights and fletchers then see stock after stock split uselessly, while freak growths in the forest announce that wood has failed in its office of bend and straight.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝正月，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: First month of Wei Emperor Wen: rain; trees iced.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Emperor Wen of Wei, rain fell and encased the trees in ice.

sentences.zh: 案劉歆說，上陽施不下通，下陰施不上達，故雨，而木為之冰，氛氣寒，木不曲直也。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xin's explanation, upper Yang operation did not penetrate downward, lower Yin operation did not ascend upward; therefore there was rain and trees became ice for it; vapor and qi were cold—wood did not bend and straighten.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin argued that Yang aloft failed to reach below while Yin below failed to rise—hence freezing rain that sheathed the branches; the air turned lethal-cold, the signature that wood had forfeited its bend-and-straight office.

sentences.zh: 劉向曰，冰者陰之盛，木者少陽，貴臣卿大夫象也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang said: Ice is the flourishing of Yin; wood is lesser Yang; it is the image of honored ministers and grand officers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang read the ice as Yin at full flood against wood's lesser Yang—the emblem of senior ministers at court.

sentences.zh: 此人將有害，則陰氣脅木，木先寒，故得雨而冰也。

translations.literal: When this person is about to suffer harm, then Yin qi coerces wood; wood first becomes cold; therefore it obtains rain and ice.
translations.idiomatic: When such an official faces mortal peril, Yin first presses upon wood's Yang; the timber turns chill before the freezing rain seals it.

sentences.zh: 是年六月，利成郡兵蔡方等殺太守徐質，據郡反。

translations.literal: That year in the sixth month, soldiers of Licheng commandery, Cai Fang and others, killed Administrator Xu Zhi and rebelled holding the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That sixth month the Licheng garrison under Cai Fang murdered Prefect Xu Zhi and seized the commandery in revolt.

sentences.zh: 太守，古之諸侯，貴臣有害之應也。

translations.literal: The administrator is the feudal lord of antiquity; it is the response of honored ministers suffering harm.
translations.idiomatic: A commandery governor ranked as a feudal lord of old—precisely the ministerial token Liu Xiang had named.

sentences.zh: 一說以木冰為木介，介者甲兵之象。

translations.literal: One explanation takes icing on trees as "wood armor"; armor is the image of weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Another gloss treats glazed branches as "armored wood," armor auguring mobilization.

sentences.zh: 是歲，既討蔡方，又八月天子自將以舟師征吳，戍卒十餘萬，連旌數百里，臨江觀兵，又屬常雨也。

translations.literal: That year, having already campaigned against Cai Fang, again in the eighth month the Son of Heaven personally led a naval force to campaign against Wu; garrison troops were over a hundred thousand, connected banners several hundred li, viewing troops along the river—it also belonged to constant rain.
translations.idiomatic: The same year saw Cai Fang crushed; then in the eighth month the emperor personally led a river fleet against Wu—more than a hundred thousand men and banners unbroken for hundreds of li massed along the bank—another spell of untimely rain.

sentences.zh: 元帝二月辛未，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, second month day xinwei: rain; trees iced.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day of Emperor Yuan's second month came freezing rain and ice-rimed trees.

sentences.zh: 後二年，周顗等遇害，是陽施不下通也。

translations.literal: After two years, Zhou Yi and others met harm—this was Yang operation not penetrating downward.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Zhou Yi and his associates were killed—the failure of Yang to extend below.

sentences.zh: 穆帝正月乙巳，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu, first month day yisi: rain; trees iced.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of Emperor Mu's first month, rain fell and trees froze over.

sentences.zh: 是年殷浩北伐，明年軍敗，十年廢黜。

translations.literal: That year Yin Hao campaigned north; the next year the army was defeated; in the tenth year he was dismissed and degraded.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao marched north that year; his army collapsed the next, and within ten years he was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 又曰，荀羨、殷浩北伐，桓溫入關之象也。

translations.literal: It is also said: Xun Xian and Yin Hao campaigned north—this was the portent of Huan Wen entering the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators also tie the sign to Xun Xian's and Yin Hao's northern expeditions—the prelude to Huan Wen's thrust into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝十二月乙巳，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, twelfth month day yisi: rain; trees iced.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of Emperor Xiaowu's twelfth month, freezing rain glazed the trees.

sentences.zh: 明年二月王恭為北籓，八月庾楷為西籓，九月王國寶為中書令，尋加領軍將軍，十七年殷仲堪為荊州，雖邪正異規，而終同夷滅，是其應也。

translations.literal: The next year second month Wang Gong became northern bulwark; eighth month Yu Kai became western bulwark; ninth month Wang Guobao became Palace Writer and soon added command of the guards; seventeenth year Yin Zhongkan became Jingzhou—although wicked and upright followed different plans, in the end alike they were exterminated together—this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Wang Gong took charge of the northern marches; by autumn Yu Kai held the western frontier and Wang Guobao entered the Palace Secretariat, soon adding command of the capital guards; within seventeen years Yin Zhongkan gained Jingzhou—rival camps clashed in principle yet every faction was annihilated alike, answering the omen.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮，諸葛恪征淮南，後所坐聽事棟中折。

translations.literal: Wu Sun Liang: when Zhuge Ke campaigned against Huainan, afterward the ridgepole of the hall where he sat broke in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Liang of Wu the central beam of Zhuge Ke's audience hall snapped after he marched against Huainan.

sentences.zh: 恪妄興征役，奪農時，作邪謀，傷國財力，故木失其性致毀折也。

translations.literal: Ke rashly raised campaigns and corvées, seized farming seasons, enacted evil plots, harmed the state's wealth and strength—therefore wood lost its nature and reached destruction and breakage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke had stirred needless wars, seized the farming calendar, and spun treasonous schemes that drained the realm—wood therefore abandoned its nature and shattered his hall.

sentences.zh: 及旋師而誅滅，于《周易》又為「棟撓之凶」也。

translations.literal: When he turned the army and was executed and extinguished, in the Zhou Changes it was again "the misfortune of a ridgepole bent."
translations.idiomatic: His retreat ended in execution and clan extinction—the Zhou yi calls such collapse the ill omen of the sagging ridgepole.

sentences.zh: 武帝五月，宣帝廟地陷，梁折。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, fifth month: the earth of Emperor Xuan's temple sank; beams broke.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wu's fifth month the floor of Emperor Xuan's temple subsided and its beams gave way.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，太廟殿又陷，改作廟，築基及泉。

translations.literal: Eighth year first month: the Grand Temple hall again sank; they rebuilt the temple, digging the foundation down to the springs.
translations.idiomatic: The first month of the eighth year brought another collapse of the imperial ancestral hall; builders dug a new foundation to the water table.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，遂更營新廟，遠致名材，雜以銅柱，陳勰為匠，作者六萬人。

translations.literal: That year ninth month: they then built anew a temple at distance, bringing celebrated timbers, mixing in bronze pillars; Chen Xie was master craftsman; those who worked were sixty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn they raised a new shrine elsewhere, importing prized lumber and bronze columns; Chen Xie directed sixty thousand laborers.

sentences.zh: 至十年四月乃成，十一月庚寅梁又折。

translations.literal: By the tenth year fourth month it was completed; eleventh month day gengyin the beams again broke.
translations.idiomatic: The structure stood finished in the tenth year's fourth month—yet on gengyin in the eleventh month the beams snapped again.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，地陷者分離之象，梁折者木不曲直也。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: sinking earth is the image of division and separation; breaking beams is wood not bending and straightening.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's lesson read partition into the sinking soil and wood's failed office into the splintered beams.

sentences.zh: 明年帝崩，而王室遂亂。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor died, and the royal house then fell into chaos.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died the next year and the Sima house slid into chaos.

sentences.zh: 惠帝，成都王穎使陸機率眾向京都，擊長沙王乂，及軍始引而牙竿折，俄而戰敗，機被誅，穎遂奔潰，卒賜死。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui: Chengdu Prince Ying had Lu Ji lead forces toward the capital to strike Changsha Prince Yi; when the army had just set out the banner pole snapped; shortly they were defeated in battle; Lu Ji was executed; Ying then fled in collapse and in the end was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui's reign: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying sent Lu Ji against Prince Changsha Sima Yi at Luoyang; the host had barely marched when the standard mast splintered—soon Lu Ji fell defeated and executed, Ying's army melted away, and Ying himself was ultimately compelled to suicide.

sentences.zh: 此奸謀之罰，木不曲直也。

translations.literal: This was the punishment for treacherous plotting—wood did not bend and straighten.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven punished the conspiracy by stripping wood of its bend-and-straight virtue.

sentences.zh: 元帝，王敦在武昌，鈴下儀仗生華如蓮華，五六日而萎落。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan: when Wang Dun was at Wuchang, halberds and paraphernalia under the guard sprouted blossoms like lotus flowers; after five or six days they withered and fell.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yuan, Wang Dun's ceremonial gear at Wuchang burst into lotus-like blooms that wilted within days.

sentences.zh: 此木失其性。

translations.literal: This was wood losing its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Wood had plainly forfeited its proper nature.

sentences.zh: 干寶以為狂華生枯木，又在鈴閣之間，言威儀之富，榮華之盛，皆如狂華之發，不可久也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao took it that mad blossoms growing on dead wood, moreover within the bell pavilion, spoke of the fullness of awe-inspiring ritual and the flourishing of glory and splendor—all like the blooming of mad blossoms, unable to endure long.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao read freak blossoms on dead timber beside the headquarters bell as an emblem of pomp and transient glory flashing as briefly as those unnatural flowers.

sentences.zh: 其後王敦終以逆命加戮其屍。

translations.literal: Afterward Wang Dun in the end by disobedient mandate had corporal punishment added to his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun later died in rebellion and suffered posthumous mutilation for defying the throne.

sentences.zh: 一說亦華孽也，于《周易》為「枯楊生華」。

translations.literal: One explanation also calls it the calamity of blossoms; in the Zhou Changes it is "withered poplar sprouts blossoms."
translations.idiomatic: Another reading classes it among floral prodigies—the Zhou yi image of fresh blossoms on a withered poplar.

sentences.zh: 桓玄始篡，龍旂竿折。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan first usurped, the dragon-banner pole snapped.
translations.idiomatic: As Huan Xuan seized the throne, the great dragon standard broke.

sentences.zh: 時玄田獵無度，飲食奢恣，土木妨農，又多奸謀，故木失其性。

translations.literal: At that time Xuan hunted without measure, ate and drank extravagantly, earth and wood works harmed farming, and there were many treacherous plots—therefore wood lost its nature.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted without restraint, feasted extravagantly, and pressed construction works that tore peasants from their fields while intrigue multiplied—wood therefore lost its nature.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，旂所以掛三辰，章著明也，旂竿之折，高明去矣。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: the banner is what hangs the three luminaries and displays brightness; breaking the banner pole means the lofty brightness departs.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven hinted that the banner displays the Three Lights of sovereignty—a shattered mast meant manifest legitimacy had departed.

sentences.zh: 玄果敗。

translations.literal: Xuan indeed was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan soon met ruin.

translations.literal: Graphical equals sign marking column alignment in the source table.
translations.idiomatic: Column spacer preserved from the tabular exemplar.

sentences.zh: 火

translations.literal: Fire.
translations.idiomatic: Fire — the southern phase.

sentences.zh: =《傳》：「棄法津，逐功臣，殺太子，以妾為妻，則火不炎上。」

translations.literal: =The Commentary: "If one casts aside law and regulation, drives off merit ministers, kills the heir-apparent, and takes a concubine as wife—then fire does not blaze upward."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary warns: "When statutes are discarded, loyal servants banished, the heir murdered, and a concubine elevated to wife, fire ceases to flame upward as it should."

sentences.zh: 說曰：火，南方，揚光輝為明者也。

translations.literal: Explanation says: Fire is the south; it raises radiance and brilliance as brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Exposition: Fire belongs to the south; its virtue is to radiate clarifying light.

sentences.zh: 其于王者，南面向明而治。

translations.literal: As for the kingly person, he faces south toward brightness and governs.
translations.idiomatic: The true king sits facing south toward the light and rules from that clarity.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：「知人則哲，能官人。

translations.literal: The Documents says: "Knowing men then wise, able to appoint men."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "To know one's ministers is to be discerning; it enables one to assign office rightly."

sentences.zh: 」故堯舜舉群賢而命之朝，遠四佞而放諸野。

translations.literal: " Therefore Yao and Shun raised the host of worthies and charged them at court, banished the four wicked men afar.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Yao and Shun summoned every worthy to court while driving the Four Fiends into distant exile.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「浸潤之譖，膚受之訴，不行焉，可謂明矣。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Insinuating slander and skin-deep accusations do not prevail—this may be called clarity."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius adds that where dripping slander and overheated accusations gain no foothold, a ruler may truly be called clear-sighted.

sentences.zh: 」賢佞分別，官人有序，帥由舊章，敬重功勳，殊別嫡庶，如此則火得其性矣。

translations.literal: " Worthies and slanderers are distinguished; appointing men has order; command follows old statutes; merit ministers are deeply respected; legitimate and concubine-born heirs are clearly differentiated—thus fire obtains its nature.
translations.idiomatic: With worthies sorted from slanderers, appointments disciplined by precedent, honors paid to true service, and succession sorted between legitimate heirs and lesser sons, fire realizes its nature.

sentences.zh: 若乃通道不篤，或耀虛偽，讒夫昌，邪勝正，則火失其性矣。

translations.literal: If then the Way is not pursued sincerely, or false glory is displayed, slanderers flourish and the deviant overcomes the upright—then fire loses its nature.
translations.idiomatic: When rulers merely toy with the Way, parade hollow virtue, empower whispering calumniators, and let deviance defeat integrity, fire abandons its nature.

sentences.zh: 自上而降，及濫炎妄起，焚宗廟，燒宮館，雖興師眾，不能救也，是為火不炎上。

translations.literal: From above downward descending, and reckless flames arise on their own, burning ancestral temples and incinerating palaces—though one raises armies in multitudes, they cannot save it—this is fire not blazing upward.
translations.idiomatic: Then rogue fire drops from on high, gutting ancestral shrines and palace halls—no host, however vast, can stamp it out; that is fire refusing to rise and illuminate as ordained.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝五月，清商殿災。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Ming, fifth month: the Qing Shang Hall caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Emperor Ming of Wei the Qing Shang Palace burned.

sentences.zh: 初，帝為平原王，納河南虞氏為妃。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor was Prince of Pingyuan, he took a Henan Yu clan woman as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while still Prince of Pingyuan, he had married a lady of the Yu clan from Henan.

sentences.zh: 及即位，不以為-{后}-，更立典虞車工卒毛嘉女為-{后}-。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he did not make her empress; he replaced her by establishing the daughter of Mao Jia, cart-maker of the Palace Coach Office, as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On accession he declined to elevate her to empress, instead enthroning the daughter of Mao Jia—a common artisan of the imperial carriage workshop—as his consort.

sentences.zh: -{后}-本仄微，非所宜升，以妾為妻之罰也。

translations.literal: The empress's origin was lowly and slight—not what was fitting to be elevated; it was the punishment of taking a concubine as wife.
translations.idiomatic: The new empress's origins were far too humble for such promotion—Heaven's rebuke for raising a concubine to wife.

sentences.zh: 六月，洛陽宮鞠室災。

translations.literal: Sixth month: the ball-court of Luoyang palace caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: The following sixth month the polo grounds inside Luoyang palace burned.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，崇華殿災，延于南閣，繕復之。

translations.literal: Second year fourth month: Chonghua Hall caught fire, extending to the southern wing; they repaired it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year Chonghua Hall burned, flames spreading to the southern annex until craftsmen rebuilt it.

sentences.zh: 至三年七月，此殿又災。

translations.literal: By third year seventh month: this hall again caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventh month of the third year the same hall was afire again.

sentences.zh: 帝問高堂隆：「此何咎也？

translations.literal: The emperor asked Gao Tanglong: "What fault is this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor demanded of Gao Tanglong: "What offense does this betoken?"

sentences.zh: 于禮寧有祈禳之義乎？

translations.literal: In rites is there indeed the meaning of prayer and exorcism?"
translations.idiomatic: Do the rites even admit prayer or apotropaic rites for such things?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「夫災變之發，皆所以明教誡也，惟率禮修德可以勝之。

translations.literal: " He replied: "As for the arising of disaster and anomaly, all are to clarify teaching and warning; only leading ritual and cultivating virtue can overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao answered: "Every calamity is Heaven's tutorial; only scrupulous ritual and cultivated virtue can master it."

sentences.zh: 《易傳》曰：『上不儉，下不節，孽火燒其室。

translations.literal: The Yi Commentary says: 'If above is not frugal and below is not restrained, baleful fire burns its chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary on the Changes warns: 'When those above forsake thrift and those below abandon restraint, baleful fire consumes the hall.'

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『君高其臺，天火為災。

translations.literal: ' It also says: 'If the lord raises his terrace high, Heaven's fire becomes disaster.'
translations.idiomatic: It adds: 'When a ruler heaps his terraces skyward, Heaven answers with consuming flame.'

sentences.zh: 』此人君苟飾宮室，不知百姓空竭，故天應之以旱，火從高殿起也。

translations.literal: ' Thus when a lord of men heedlessly adorns palace chambers and does not know that the hundred clans are emptied and exhausted, Heaven responds to him with drought, and fire arises from the lofty halls.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler bankrupts his people to gild his halls, Heaven answers with drought and sends flame sweeping down from the highest roofs.

sentences.zh: 案《舊占》曰：『災火之發，皆以臺榭宮室為誡。

translations.literal: According to the Old Prognostications it says: 'The outbreak of calamitous fire always takes towers, pavilions, palaces and chambers as its warning.'
translations.idiomatic: The Old Prognostications record that destructive fire always singles out palace terraces and halls as its cautionary targets.

sentences.zh: 』今宜罷散作役，務從節約，清掃所災之處，不敢於此有所營造，萐莆嘉禾必生此地，以報陛下虔恭之德。

translations.literal: ' Now it is fitting to dismiss and scatter labor duties, strive to follow austerity, cleanse and sweep the places that suffered disaster, not dare here to undertake construction—shanfu grass and auspicious grain will surely spring from this ground to repay Your Majesty's reverent and respectful virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Suspend every levy, embrace austerity, clear the charred ground, and raise nothing new upon it—auspicious grain and ritual plants will spring up there to reward your sober piety.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brushed the counsel aside.

sentences.zh: 遂復崇華殿，改曰九龍。

translations.literal: Thereupon they rebuilt Chonghua Hall and changed its name to Nine Dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua Hall rose again, rechristened the Nine Dragons Palace.

sentences.zh: 以郡國前後言龍見者九，故以為名。

translations.literal: Because commanderies and kingdoms before and after reported dragon sightings numbering nine, they took this as its name.
translations.idiomatic: Nine regional reports of dragon sightings supplied the new name.

sentences.zh: 多棄法度，疲眾逞欲，以妾為妻之應也。

translations.literal: Much casting aside law and measure, exhausting the masses and indulging desires—it was the response of taking a concubine as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Law lay in ruins, the people were driven past endurance, and private appetite ruled—all Heaven's echo of elevating a concubine to wife.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮十二月，武昌端門災，改作，端門又災。

translations.literal: Wu Sun Liang, twelfth month: Wuchang's Main Gate caught fire; they rebuilt it, and the Main Gate again caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In Sun Liang's twelfth month Wuchang's ceremonial gate burned; rebuilt, it burned again.

sentences.zh: 內殿門者，號令所出；

translations.literal: The gate of the inner hall is where commands issue forth;
translations.idiomatic: The inner hall gate is where imperial commands depart;

sentences.zh: 殿者，聽政之所。

translations.literal: the hall is the place of hearing governance.
translations.idiomatic: the hall itself is where policy is heard and settled.

sentences.zh: 是時諸葛恪執政，而矜慢放肆，孫峻總禁旅，而險害終著。

translations.literal: At this time Zhuge Ke held government and was arrogant, negligent and unrestrained; Sun Jun commanded the palace troops, yet treacherous harm in the end manifested plainly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke dominated court yet swaggered beyond restraint; Sun Jun controlled the capital guard and nursed malice that soon surfaced.

sentences.zh: 武昌，孫氏尊號所始。

translations.literal: Wuchang is where the Sun clan's honored title began.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang was the cradle of Sun Wu's kingship.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，宜除其貴要之首者，恪果喪眾殄人，峻授政於綝，綝廢亮也。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say one should remove him who is chief among the honored and powerful; Ke indeed lost the host and extinguished men; Jun handed government to Lin; Lin deposed Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven hinted at cutting down the paramount lord—Zhuge Ke fell and brought slaughter; Sun Jun yielded power to Sun Lin, who then cast Sun Liang aside.

sentences.zh: 或曰，孫權毀撤武昌以增太初宮，諸葛恪有遷都意，更起門殿，事非時宜，故見災也。

translations.literal: Some say: Sun Quan demolished and withdrew Wuchang to enlarge Taichu Palace; Zhuge Ke had the intention to move the capital and rebuilt gate-halls—the affair was untimely, therefore disaster appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Others blame Sun Quan's dismantling of Wuchang to expand Taichu Palace and Zhuge Ke's scheme to shift the capital—untimely construction drew Heaven's fire.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「君不思道，厥妖火燒宮。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yi Commentary says: "If the lord does not ponder the Way, its anomaly is fire burning the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's commentary warns that when a ruler abandons the Way, flame consumes his palace.

sentences.zh: 二月朔，建鄴火，人之火也。

translations.literal: Second month new moon: Jianye caught fire—it was fire caused by men.
translations.idiomatic: On the second month's new moon Jianye burned—human hands, not Heaven, lit it.

sentences.zh: 是秋，孫綝始執政，矯以亮詔殺呂據、滕胤。

translations.literal: That autumn Sun Lin first held government and falsely used Liang's edict to kill Lu Ju and Teng Yin.
translations.idiomatic: That fall Sun Lin seized power and forged Sun Liang's order to execute Lu Ju and Teng Yin.

sentences.zh: 明年，又輒殺硃異。

translations.literal: The next year, again on his own authority he killed Zhu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he murdered Zhu Yi without sanction.

sentences.zh: 棄法律逐功臣之罰也。

translations.literal: It was the punishment of casting aside laws and driving off merit ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's penalty for tearing up statute and purging loyal servants.

sentences.zh: 孫休二月，城西門北樓災。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu, second month: the north tower at the city's west gate caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In Sun Xiu's second month fire consumed the north tower on the western gate.

sentences.zh: 六年十月，石頭小城火，燒西南百八十丈。

translations.literal: Sixth year tenth month: Shitou minor citadel caught fire, burning one hundred eighty zhang on the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth month of the sixth year saw Shitou fortress burn along a hundred eighty zhang of its southwest wall.

sentences.zh: 是時嬖人張布專擅國勢，多行無禮，而韋昭、盛沖終斥不用，兼遣察戰等為內史，驚擾州郡，致使交趾反亂，是其咎也。

translations.literal: At this time favorite Zhang Bu monopolized state power and frequently acted without propriety, while Wei Zhao and Sheng Chong were in the end dismissed and not employed; moreover dispatching investigators such as Zha Zhan as interior clerks alarmed and disturbed provinces and commanderies, causing Jiaozhi to rebel and riot—this was its fault.
translations.idiomatic: The favorite Zhang Bu hijacked government with systematic rudeness while scholars like Wei Zhao and Sheng Chong languished in disgrace; inspectors terrorized the provinces until Jiaozhi rose in revolt—the fitting sequel.

sentences.zh: 孫皓三月，大火，燒萬餘家，死者七百人。

translations.literal: Sun Hao, third month: great fire; burned over ten thousand households; seven hundred dead.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's third month brought a conflagration that gutted ten thousand homes and killed seven hundred souls.

sentences.zh: 案《春秋》齊大災，劉向以為桓公好內，聽女口，妻妾數更之罰也。

translations.literal: According to the Spring and Autumn, Qi suffered great disaster; Liu Xiang took it that Duke Huan favored the inner quarters, listened to women's mouths, and repeatedly replaced wives and concubines—the punishment thereof.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi inferno recorded in the Annals Liu Xiang read as Duke Huan's harem politics—women's whispered counsel and ever-shifting favorites inviting Heaven's blaze.

sentences.zh: 時皓制令詭暴，蕩棄法度，勞臣名士，誅斥甚眾，後宮萬餘，女謁數行，其中隆寵佩皇后璽綬者又多矣，故有大火。

translations.literal: At that time Hao's regulations and commands were deceitful and cruel, sweeping aside law and measure; toiling ministers and celebrated gentlemen were many executed and dismissed; the rear palace exceeded ten thousand; women's solicitations passed repeatedly; among them those greatly favored wearing empress seals and cords were again numerous—therefore there was great fire.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's capricious cruelty hollowed out law, purged countless ministers, and stuffed the harem past ten thousand women whose intrigues ran unchecked—many bore regalia fit for an empress—so the capital caught flame.

sentences.zh: 武帝三月乙丑，震災西閣楚王所止坊及臨商觀窗。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, third month day yichou: lightning struck the western wing—the ward where the Prince of Chu lodged and the windows of the Linshang Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in Emperor Wu's third month lightning shattered the Prince of Chu's western annex and the Linshang Observatory's casements.

sentences.zh: 十年四月癸丑，崇賢殿災。

translations.literal: Tenth year fourth month day guichou: Chongxian Hall caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxian Hall burned on guichou in the tenth year's fourth month.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚辰，含章鞠室、修成堂前廡、景坊東屋、暉章殿南閣火。

translations.literal: Eleventh month day gengchen: Hanzhang ball-court, the porches before Xiucheng Hall, the eastern chambers of Jing Ward, and the southern wing of Huizhang Hall caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen in the eleventh month flame raced through the polo grounds at Hanzhang, Xiucheng Hall's front galleries, Jing Ward's east rooms, and Huizhang Hall's south pavilion.

sentences.zh: 時有上書曰：「漢王氏五侯，兄弟迭任，今楊氏三公，並在大位，故天變屢見，竊為陛下憂之。

translations.literal: At the time someone submitted a memorial saying: "Han Wang clan's five marquises, brothers alternating in office—now Yang clan's three dukes together hold great positions; therefore celestial anomalies repeatedly appear—I privately worry for Your Majesty on this account."
translations.idiomatic: A memorial warned that Han's Wang quintet had rotated power among brothers while today's Yang triumvirate monopolized the highest posts—hence Heaven's repeated warnings.

sentences.zh: 」由是楊珧求退。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yang Yao sought to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yao promptly petitioned to resign.

sentences.zh: 是時帝納馮紞之間，廢張華之功，聽楊駿之讒，離衛瓘之寵，此逐功臣之罰也。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor accepted Feng Dan's alienation, discarded Zhang Hua's achievements, listened to Yang Jun's slander, and estranged Wei Guan's favor—this was the punishment of driving off merit ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The throne swallowed Feng Dan's intrigues, erased Zhang Hua's merit, heeded Yang Jun's malice, and spurned Wei Guan—exactly the crime of banishing loyal servants.

sentences.zh: 明年，宮車宴駕。

translations.literal: The next year, the palace carriage feasted its ascent.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor died—the euphemism for the imperial hearse departing forever.

sentences.zh: 其後楚王承竊發之旨，戮害二公，身亦不免。

translations.literal: Afterward the Prince of Chu received secret issued orders, slaughtered and harmed the two dukes, and his person also did not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Then Prince Chu, acting on clandestine orders, murdered both elder statesmen yet could not save himself.

sentences.zh: 震災其坊，又天意乎。

translations.literal: Lightning struck his ward—was it again Heaven's intent?
translations.idiomatic: Lightning scarred his precinct—another cipher of Heaven's will?

sentences.zh: 惠帝閏月庚寅，武庫火。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui, intercalary month day gengyin: the armory caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin in the intercalary month of Emperor Hui's reign the imperial arsenal burned.

sentences.zh: 張華疑有亂，先命固守，然後救火。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua suspected there was turmoil; first he ordered steadfast defense, afterward fought the fire.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua feared revolt and sealed the depot before allowing anyone to fight the flames.

sentences.zh: 是以累代異寶，王莽頭，孔子屐，漢高祖斷白蛇劍及二百八萬器械，一時蕩盡。

translations.literal: Therefore generation after generation of strange treasures, Wang Mang's head, Confucius's sandal, Han Gaozu's sword that cut the white serpent, and two million eight hundred thousand weapons and gear—in one moment were utterly swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Treasures hoarded across dynasties—Wang Mang's skull, Confucius's shoe, Gaozu's serpent-slaying blade, nearly three million weapons—vanished in an afternoon.

sentences.zh: 是後湣懷太子見殺之罰也。

translations.literal: Afterward it was the punishment of Crown Prince Minhuai being killed.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven foreshadowed the murder of Crown Prince Minhuai.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，夫設險擊柝，所以固其國，儲積戒器，所以戒不虞。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: establishing defenses and striking night-watch rattles is how one secures the state; storing and accumulating guard weapons is how one guards against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven warned that ramparts and night patrols secure a realm while arsenals hedge against surprise—yet both were reduced to ash.

sentences.zh: 今塚嗣將傾，社稷將泯，禁兵無所復施，皇旅又將誰衛。

translations.literal: Now the heir at the tomb-shrine is about to topple, altars of soil and grain are about to vanish—palace troops have nowhere again to be deployed; imperial hosts again will guard whom?
translations.idiomatic: The heir totters, the altars face extinction, palace guards lose their arms, and no loyal host remains to shield the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝后不悟，終喪四海，是其應也。

translations.literal: Emperor and empress did not awaken; in the end they lost the four seas—this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: Throne and consort ignored the lesson and forfeited the realm—the fitting aftermath.

sentences.zh: 張華、閻纂皆曰，武庫火而氐羌反，太子見廢，則四海可知。」

translations.literal: Zhang Hua and Yan Zuan both said: When the armory burns and Di and Qiang rebel, and the crown prince is seen deposed—then the four seas may be known."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua and Yan Zuan warned that burning arsenals, Di-Qiang revolt, and a deposed heir spelled empire-wide collapse.

sentences.zh: 八年十一月，高原陵火。

translations.literal: Eighth year eleventh month: Gaoyuan Mausoleum caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyuan tumulus burned in the eighth year's eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 是時賈后凶恣，賈謐擅朝，惡積罪稔，宜見誅絕。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Jia was fierce and unrestrained; Jia Mi monopolized court; evil accumulated and guilt ripened—they deserved to be executed and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia ravaged the palace while Jia Mi hijacked government—crimes piled high enough to merit extinction.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，臣妾之不可者，雖親貴莫比，猶宜忍而誅之，如吾燔高原陵也。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: concubines who are impermissible—even if intimate and noble beyond compare—still should be endured and executed, as I burn Gaoyuan Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven signaled that even the emperor's favorite kin must face the axe—as when lightning scorched Gaoyuan's mound.

sentences.zh: 帝既眊弱，而張華又不納裴頠、劉卞之謀，故後遂與謐殺太子也。

translations.literal: The emperor was already dim and weak, and Zhang Hua again did not accept Pei Yi and Liu Bian's plots—therefore afterward she together with Mi killed the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The feeble emperor dithered while Zhang Hua spurned Pei Yi and Liu Bian's plots—so Empress Jia and Jia Mi murdered the heir.

sentences.zh: 干寶以為「高原陵火，太子廢之應。

translations.literal: Gan Bao took it that "Gaoyuan Mausoleum fire is the response to the crown prince's deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao read the tomb fire as Heaven's verdict on the heir's deposition.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝世，高園便殿火，董仲舒對與此占同」。

translations.literal: In Han Emperor Wu's era Gaoyuan side-hall caught fire; Dong Zhongshu's response matched this prognostication in this."
translations.idiomatic: He cited Emperor Wu's blaze at Gaoyuan's annex—Dong Zhongshu had read it the same way.

sentences.zh: ，帝納皇后羊氏，-{后}-將入宮，衣中忽有火，眾咸怪之。

translations.literal: The emperor took Empress Yang clan as empress; when the empress was about to enter the palace, fire suddenly appeared in her garments—all wondered at it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui welcomed Empress Yang, flame burst from her robes as she crossed the threshold—a marvel to every witness.

sentences.zh: ，成都王遂廢-{后}-，處之金墉城。

translations.literal: Chengdu Prince thereupon deposed the empress and placed her in Jinyong Citadel.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chengdu soon deposed her and immured her at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 是後還立，立而復廢者四。

translations.literal: Afterward she was restored and established; established and again deposed—four times.
translations.idiomatic: She was enthroned, cast down, restored, and stripped again—four wrenching cycles.

sentences.zh: 又詔賜死，荀籓表全之。

translations.literal: Again an edict ordered her forced to die; Xun Fan memorialized to preserve her.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict demanded her death until Xun Fan's plea spared her.

sentences.zh: 雖來還在位，然憂逼折辱，終古未聞。

translations.literal: Although she came back and still held position, yet anxiety pressed and humiliation broke her—never heard of from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Even when briefly restored she endured humiliation unparalleled in memory.

sentences.zh: 此孽火之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response of baleful fire.
translations.idiomatic: The robe-fire had warned of every outrage that followed.

sentences.zh: 七月甲午，尚書諸曹火起，延崇禮闥及閣道。

translations.literal: Seventh month day jiawu: fire arose in the various bureaus of the Masters of Writing, extending to Chongli portals and gallery passages.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu in the seventh month flame leaped through the Secretariat, racing to Chongli Gate and the aerial corridors.

sentences.zh: 夫百揆王化之本，王者棄法津之應也。

translations.literal: Now the hundred administrators are root of kingly transformation—it was the response of the kingly person casting aside law and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries anchor civilization itself—the blaze mirrored the monarch's contempt for law.

sentences.zh: 後清河王覃入嗣，不終於位，又殺太子之罰也。

translations.literal: Afterward Prince Qinghe Tan entered as heir but did not finish in position—it was again the punishment of killing the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qinghe Sima Tan briefly succeeded yet fell—Heaven's further reckoning for slaying the heir.

sentences.zh: 孝懷帝十一月，襄陽火，燒死者三千餘人。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohuai, eleventh month: Xiangyang caught fire; burned dead exceeded three thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaohuai's eleventh month saw Xiangyang burn with three thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 是時王如自號大將軍、司雍二州牧，眾四五萬，攻略郡縣。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Ru styled himself Grand General and shepherd of Si and Yong two provinces; hosts forty or fifty thousand raided and attacked commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru styled himself generalissimo and governor of Si-Yong at the head of forty or fifty thousand bandits pillaging every county.

sentences.zh: 此下陵上，陽失其節之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response of inferiors encroaching on superiors, Yang losing its measure.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners overawed their betters—Yang energy slipped its reins.

sentences.zh: 元帝太興中，王敦鎮武昌，武昌災，火起，興眾救之，救於此而發於彼，東西南北數十處俱應，數日不絕。

translations.literal: Within Emperor Yuan's Taixing era Wang Dun garrisoned Wuchang; Wuchang suffered disaster; fire arose; they raised multitudes to rescue it—they rescued here yet it broke out there; east, west, south, north several tens of places simultaneously responded; several days it did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Dun held Wuchang during Taixing, freak fires erupted in dozens of spots at once—soldiers smothered one blaze only to see another ignite, for days without end.

sentences.zh: 舊說所謂「濫炎妄起，雖興師眾，不能救之」之謂也。

translations.literal: This is what old explanations call "reckless flames arising wildly—though one raises armies in multitudes, one cannot save them."
translations.idiomatic: Classic glosses call it rampant flame no army can quench.

sentences.zh: 干寶以為「此臣而君行，亢陽失節，是為王敦陵上，有無君之心，故災也。」

translations.literal: Gan Bao took it that "this is minister acting lord's role, arrogant Yang losing measure—it is Wang Dun encroaching on superiors, harboring a heart without lord—therefore disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao diagnosed minister usurping monarch, Yang run riot—Wang Dun's treason inviting Heaven's fire.

sentences.zh: 正月癸巳，京師大火。

translations.literal: First month day guisi: the capital suffered great fire.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi in the first month the capital burned fiercely.

sentences.zh: 三月，饒安、東光、安陵三縣火，燒七千餘家，死者萬五千人。

translations.literal: Third month: Rao'an, Dongguang, and Anling three counties caught fire; burned over seven thousand households; dead ten thousand five hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: March brought firestorms across Rao'an, Dongguang, and Anling—seven thousand homes lost and fifteen thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 明帝正月，京都火。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, first month: the capital caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming's first month saw the metropolis burn.

sentences.zh: 是時王敦威侮朝廷，多行無禮，內外臣下咸懷怨毒，極陰生陽也。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Dun threatened and insulted court, frequently acted without propriety; inner and outer ministers all harbored resentment and poison—extreme Yin engendered Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun bullied the throne until spite filled every minister—Yin pressed so hard it burst into fiery Yang.

sentences.zh: 成帝五月，京師火。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng, fifth month: the capital caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng's fifth month brought another capital blaze.

sentences.zh: 康帝七月庚申，吳郡災。

translations.literal: Emperor Kang, seventh month day gengshen: Wu commandery suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in Emperor Kang's seventh month Wu commandery burned.

sentences.zh: 穆帝六月，震災石季龍太武殿及兩廟端門。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu, sixth month: lightning struck Shi Jilong's Taiwu Hall and both temples' main gates.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu's sixth month saw lightning blast Shi Hu's Taiwu Palace and the twin ancestral gates.

sentences.zh: 震災月餘乃滅，金石皆盡。

translations.literal: The lightning disaster over a month then was extinguished; metal and stone were all consumed.
translations.idiomatic: The strikes raged more than a month until bronze and stone melted away.

sentences.zh: 其後季龍死，大亂，遂滅亡。

translations.literal: Afterward Jilong died, great chaos, thereupon perished and was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu died soon after, plunging Later Zhao into ruin.

sentences.zh: 海西公太和中，郗愔為會稽太守。

translations.literal: Within Duke of Haixi's Taihe era Xi Yin was Kuaiji administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Under the deposed Duke of Haixi, Xi Yin governed Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 六月大旱災，火燒數千家。

translations.literal: Sixth month great drought disaster; fire burned several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: June drought fed flames that consumed thousands of homes.

sentences.zh: 延及山陰倉米數百萬斛，炎煙蔽天，不可撲滅。

translations.literal: It extended to Shanyin granary grain several million hu; blazing smoke hid the sky; could not be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Fire swallowed millions of hu of grain at Shanyin's granaries under smoke-choked skies none could fight.

sentences.zh: 此亦桓溫強盛，將廢海西，極陰生陽之應也。

translations.literal: This again was Huan Wen strong and flourishing, about to depose Duke of Haixi—response of extreme Yin engendering Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators tied it to Huan Wen's ascent and his coming deposition of Duke Haixi—Yin yielding explosive Yang.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝三月，京師風火大起。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, third month: wind-fire greatly arose in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu's third month brought wind-driven firestorms through the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時桓溫入朝，志在陵上，少主踐位，人懷憂恐，此與太寧火事同。

translations.literal: At this time Huan Wen entered court, his aim set on encroaching on superiors; the young lord mounted the throne; people harbored worry and fear—this matches the Taining fire affair.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen marched on Luoyang while the boy emperor trembled on the throne—anxiety matched Taining-era omens.

sentences.zh: 正月，國子學生因風放火，焚房百餘間。

translations.literal: First month: Imperial Academy students took advantage of wind to set fire; burned over a hundred rooms.
translations.idiomatic: First-month winds let academy students torch more than a hundred chambers.

sentences.zh: 是後考課不厲，賞黜無章。

translations.literal: Afterward examinations were not severe; rewards and dismissals lacked pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward examinations slackened and promotions followed no discernible rule.

sentences.zh: 蓋有育才之名，而無收賢之實，此不哲之罰先兆也。

translations.literal: Generally there was the name of fostering talent but not the reality of gathering worthies—this was precursor of punishment for lack of clarity.
translations.idiomatic: The school cultivated talent in name alone—the first tremor of Heaven's sentence on benighted rule.

sentences.zh: 十三年十二月乙未，延賢堂災。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year twelfth month day yiwei: Yancian Hall caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: Yancian Hall burned on yiwei in the thirteenth year's twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 是月丙申，螽斯則百堂及客館、驃騎府庫皆災。

translations.literal: That month day bingshen: Zhongsi Zepai Hall together with guest lodges and Cavalry General's armory all caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the same month flame swept the Zhongsi Zepai hall, state guesthouses, and the guard general's depot.

sentences.zh: 于時朝多弊政，衰陵日兆，不哲之罰，皆有象類。

translations.literal: At that time court had many corrupt policies; decline daily showed omens; punishments for lack of clarity all had images and categories.
translations.idiomatic: Court rot grew daily manifest—every ill omen mirrored Heaven's reproach of blind rule.

sentences.zh: 主相不悟，終至亂亡。

translations.literal: Lord and minister did not awaken; in the end reached chaos and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Throne and regent ignored the signs until collapse followed.

sentences.zh: 會稽王道子寵倖尼及姏母，各樹用其親戚，乃至出入宮掖，禮見人主。

translations.literal: Prince Kuaiji Daozi favored nuns and aged nurses; each planted and employed their kin; reaching to entering and exiting palace women's quarters, ritual-audience with lord of men.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kuaiji Wang Daozi pampered nuns and nursemaids who installed their kin inside the harem with ceremonial audiences before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，登延賢堂及客館者多非其人，故災之也。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: those who ascend Yancian Hall and guest lodges are mostly not the right persons—therefore it disasters them.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven hinted that unworthy men thronged the halls reserved for worthies—so fire purged them.

sentences.zh: 又，孝武帝更不立皇后，寵倖微賤張夫人，夫人驕妒，皇子不繁，乖「螽斯則百」之道，故災其殿焉。

translations.literal: Moreover Emperor Xiaowu further did not establish empress; favored lowly Lady Zhang; the lady was arrogant and jealous; imperial sons were not numerous—contrary to the way of "zhongsi zebai"—therefore it disastered her hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu never named an empress but exalted the humble Lady Zhang, whose jealousy thinned the imperial nursery—violating the ode's prayer for teeming heirs—so flame consumed her hall.

sentences.zh: 道子復賞賜不節，故府庫被災，斯亦其罰也。

translations.literal: Daozi again bestowed rewards without measure—therefore armories suffered disaster; this too was its punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daozi's reckless patronage emptied treasuries—and fire answered.

sentences.zh: 安帝三月，龍舟二乘災，是水沴火也。

translations.literal: Emperor An, third month: two dragon boats suffered disaster—this was water encroaching on fire.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An's third month consumed two imperial barges—water's imbalance quenching fire.

sentences.zh: 其後桓玄篡位，帝乃播越。

translations.literal: Afterward Huan Xuan usurped the throne; the emperor then wandered in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan's coup soon drove the emperor into wandering exile.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，王者流遷，不復禦龍舟，故災之耳。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: the kingly person drifts and shifts, no longer rides dragon boats—therefore it disasters them.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven hinted that a throne adrift no longer commands the dragon barges—so they burned.

sentences.zh: 八月庚子，尚書下舍曹火。

translations.literal: Eighth month day gengzi: fire in the Masters of Writing lower quarters bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat's lower offices burned on gengzi in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 時桓玄遙錄尚書，故天火，示不復居也。

translations.literal: At that time Huan Xuan remotely recorded Masters of Writing—therefore Heaven fire, showing no longer to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan held the Secretariat by remote control—Heaven's lightning declared the office uninhabitable.

sentences.zh: 三年，盧循攻略廣州，刺史吳隱之閉城固守。

translations.literal: Third year: Lu Xun raided and attacked Guangzhou; Inspector Wu Yinshi closed the city and firmly defended.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Lu Xun besieged Guangzhou while Wu Yinshi barred the gates.

sentences.zh: 其十月壬戌夜，火起。

translations.literal: That tenth month day renxu night: fire arose.
translations.idiomatic: Fire broke out on renxu night in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 時百姓避寇盈滿城內，隱之懼有應賊者，但務嚴兵，不先救火。

translations.literal: At the time common people avoiding bandits filled the city inside; Yinshi feared there were those who would respond to bandits; only strove to tighten troops, did not first fight fire.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees packed the walls while Wu Yinshi feared collaborators and marshaled guards instead of firefighters.

sentences.zh: 由是府舍焚蕩，燒死者萬餘人，因遂散潰，悉為賊擒。

translations.literal: Thereby government buildings burned away; burned dead exceeded ten thousand persons; thereupon they scattered and collapsed—all were captured by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Official quarters became pyres; ten thousand perished; defenses collapsed and Lu Xun seized everyone.

sentences.zh: 七月丁酉，尚書殿中吏部曹火。

translations.literal: Seventh month day dingyou: fire in Masters of Writing palace interior Personnel bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The Personnel bureau inside the Secretariat burned on dingyou in the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 九年，京都大火，燒數千家。

translations.literal: Ninth year: capital great fire; burned several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth year brought a capital inferno devouring thousands of homes.

sentences.zh: 十一年，京都所在大行火災，吳界尤甚。

translations.literal: Eleventh year: wherever the capital stood, great fires spread; the Wu lands suffered worst.
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh year brought capital-wide infernos, most severe throughout Wu.

sentences.zh: 火防甚峻，猶自不絕。

translations.literal: Fire precautions were extremely strict, yet the outbreaks still did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Even draconian fire watches failed to halt the flames.

sentences.zh: 王弘時為吳郡，晝在聽事，見天上有一赤物下，狀如信幡，遙集路南人家屋上，火即大發。

translations.literal: Wang Hong then administered Wu commandery; during daylight in the audience hall he saw a red object descend from the sky like a credential-banner; from afar it settled on a rooftop south of the road, and fire immediately erupted.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wang Hong watched a crimson banner-like mass drift from the sky onto a roof—and instant blaze followed.

sentences.zh: 弘知天為之災，故不罪火主。

translations.literal: Hong knew Heaven had wrought the disaster; therefore he did not punish the homeowner.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing Heaven's hand, Wang Hong spared the householder any blame.

sentences.zh: 此帝室衰微之應也。

translations.literal: This was the portent of the imperial house's decline.
translations.idiomatic: It foretold the dynasty's fading mandate.

sentences.zh: 土

translations.literal: Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Earth — the central phase.

sentences.zh: =《傳》曰：「修宮室，飾臺榭，內淫亂，犯親戚，侮兄弟，則稼穡不成。」

translations.literal: =The Commentary says: "If one repairs palace chambers, adorns terraces and pavilions, indulges inner debauchery, offends kin by marriage, insults brothers—then sowing and reaping do not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: The gloss warns that lavish inner palaces, moral chaos between spouses and siblings, and neglected farmers doom the harvest.

sentences.zh: 說曰：土，中央，生萬物者也。

translations.literal: Explanation says: Earth is the center; it bears the myriad things into life.
translations.idiomatic: Exposition: Earth occupies the center and brings forth all creatures.

sentences.zh: 其于王者，為內事，宮室、夫婦、親屬，亦相生者也。

translations.literal: For royal affairs it signifies inner governance—palaces, husbands and wives, agnates—and their mutual fostering.
translations.idiomatic: State ritual begins at home: halls, marriage ties, and kin networks must nourish one another.

sentences.zh: 古者天子諸侯，宮廟大小高卑有制，-{后}-夫人媵妾多少有度，九族親疏長幼有序。

translations.literal: Anciently Son of Heaven and feudal lords regulated the size and height of temples and halls; empress, principal wives, and secondary consorts had fixed numbers; the nine kinships ranked closeness and seniority.
translations.idiomatic: Classical kings capped shrine dimensions, limited consorts by rank, and ordered the nine branches of kin.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「禮，與其奢也，寧儉。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "In ritual, rather than extravagance, better frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius taught that spare simplicity beats lavish ritual.

sentences.zh: 」故禹卑宮室，文王刑于寡妻，此聖人之所以昭教化也。

translations.literal: " Therefore Yu built low halls; King Wen disciplined himself before his few wives—such is how sages broadcast moral instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Yu kept his palace humble and King Wen modeled virtue for his household—the sage pattern for transforming the realm.

sentences.zh: 如此，則土得其性矣。

translations.literal: Thus earth realizes its proper nature.
translations.idiomatic: Then earth fulfills its appointed office.

sentences.zh: 若乃奢淫驕慢，則土失其性。

translations.literal: If instead there is extravagance, licentiousness, arrogance, and sloth—earth loses its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagance, lust, pride, and indolence strip earth of its virtue.

sentences.zh: 亡水旱之災而草木百穀不熟，是為稼穡不成。

translations.literal: Though flood and drought do not strike, grasses, trees, and grains fail to ripen—this is harvest not succeeding.
translations.idiomatic: Without flood or drought the crops still refuse to ripen—the failure called 'grain does not finish.'

sentences.zh: 吳孫皓時，常歲無水旱，苗稼豐美而實不成，百姓以饑，闔境皆然，連歲不已。

translations.literal: Under Wu's Sun Hao ordinary years lacked floods or droughts; seedlings flourished yet kernels never formed; commoners starved; the entire realm suffered year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's reign saw freak seasons: lush fields that yielded empty ears and famine coast to coast.

sentences.zh: 吳人以為傷露，非也。

translations.literal: Wu folk blamed injured dew—that was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu gossip blamed 'scorched dew,' but the treatise rejects that reading.

sentences.zh: 案劉向《春秋說》曰「水旱當書，不書水旱而曰大無麥禾者，土氣不養，稼穡不成」，此其義也。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's Spring and Autumn Explanation: "Flood and drought ought to be recorded; when the classic instead says great absence of wheat and grain, earth qi fails to nourish—grain does not ripen"—that captures the sense.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang explained that missing grain entries signal earth refusing to nurture seed—a drought of another kind.

sentences.zh: 皓初遷都武昌，尋還建鄴，又起新館，綴飾珠玉，壯麗過甚，破壞諸營，增廣苑囿，犯暑妨農，官私疲怠。

translations.literal: When Hao first shifted the capital to Wuchang he soon returned to Jianye; again he raised new lodges inlaid with pearls and jades, grandeur exceeding measure; demolished camps; enlarged hunting parks; offended the summer heat and harmed farming—officials and commoners alike collapsed from exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's restless building—fine veneers, shattered barracks, swollen parks—wrecked harvests and exhausted everyone.

sentences.zh: 《月令》，季夏不可以興土功，

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances forbid earthworks in the final summer month—
translations.idiomatic: The ritual calendar bans groundbreaking in late summer—

sentences.zh: 皓皆冒之。

translations.literal: —yet Hao violated every prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: —yet Hao flouted every rule.

sentences.zh: 此修宮室飾臺榭之罰也。

translations.literal: This was Heaven's penalty for repairing palaces and decking terraces.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven punished his palace extravagance.

sentences.zh: 元帝，吳郡、吳興、東陽無麥禾，大饑。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan: Wu commandery, Wuxing, and Wudong lacked wheat and grain—great famine.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan's reign starved Wu, Wuxing, and Wudong of wheat.

sentences.zh: 成帝，無麥禾，天下大饑。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng: no wheat or grain—great famine across the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng the empire-wide wheat crop failed.

sentences.zh: 穆帝，三麥不登。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu: three wheat crops failed to ripen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu watched three successive wheat harvests collapse.

sentences.zh: 十二年，大無麥。

translations.literal: Twelfth year: great absence of wheat.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth year brought total wheat failure.

sentences.zh: 孝武，無麥禾，天下大饑。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu: no wheat or grain—great famine across the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu's reign repeated the empire-wide grain disaster.

sentences.zh: 安帝，無麥禾，天下大饑。

translations.literal: Emperor An: no wheat or grain—great famine across the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An faced the same catastrophic dearth.
