sentences.zh: 金

translations.literal: Metal.
translations.idiomatic: Metal — the western phase.

sentences.zh: =《傳》曰：「好戰攻，輕百姓，飾城郭，侵邊境，則金不從革。」

translations.literal: =The Commentary says: "If one loves attacking and warfare, slights the hundred clans, adorns city walls, encroaches on frontiers—then metal does not obey transformation."
translations.idiomatic: The gloss ties militarism, abusive labor on ramparts, and border raids to metal's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 說曰：金，西方，萬物既成，殺氣之始也。

translations.literal: Explanation says: Metal is the west; myriad things are finished there—beginning of killing qi.
translations.idiomatic: West belongs to metal where creation ends and autumn's killing breath begins.

sentences.zh: 故立秋而鷹隼擊，秋分而微霜降。

translations.literal: Therefore at Beginning of Autumn hawks and falcons strike; at Autumn Equinox slight frost descends.
translations.idiomatic: Hence ritual autumn opens with raptors on the hunt and ends with first frost.

sentences.zh: 其于王事，出軍行師，把旄杖鉞，誓士眾，抗威武，所以征叛逆，止暴亂也。

translations.literal: For royal affairs: marching armies and hosts; grasping yak-banner and wielding axe; swearing the ranks; displaying martial awe—these punish rebellion and halt violence.
translations.idiomatic: War lies in metal's sphere: banners, axes, oaths, and awe rightly crush traitors.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「有虔執鉞，如火烈烈。

translations.literal: The Odes says: "With solemn awe they grasp the axe—blazing like fire.
translations.idiomatic: The Canon pictures warriors gripping bronze axes in fiery discipline.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「載戢干戈，載橐弓矢。

translations.literal: " Also says: "Then bundle shields and spears, then bag bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Peace stores shields, spears, bows, and arrows away.

sentences.zh: 」動靜應宜，說以犯難，人忘其死，金得其性矣。

translations.literal: " Movement and stillness properly answered; persuasion through braving hardship—men forget death—metal obtains its nature.
translations.idiomatic: When force serves measured ends soldiers forget fear—metal stays true.

sentences.zh: 若乃貪欲恣睢，務立威勝，不重人命，則金失其性。

translations.literal: If greed runs rampant, might alone is prized, and lives count for nothing—metal loses its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Ruthless ambition that wastes lives corrupts metal.

sentences.zh: 蓋工冶鑄金鐵，冰滯涸堅，不成者眾，乃為變怪，是為金不從革。

translations.literal: Then smithies casting bronze and iron freeze, jam, and refuse to take shape—prodigies multiply—this is metal refusing transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Forgeries twist in the forge; ore rebels—that is metal spurning its office.

sentences.zh: 魏時張掖石瑞，雖是晉之符命，而于魏為妖。

translations.literal: Wei-era Zhangye stone omens were Jin's mandate tokens yet counted as Wei prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: Those Zhangye stones augured Jin's rise yet haunted Wei as anomalies.

sentences.zh: 好攻戰，輕百姓，飾城郭，侵邊境，魏氏三祖皆有其事。

translations.literal: Love of war, contempt for subjects, gilded ramparts, border raids—all three Wei founders practiced them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao warlords indulged every offense the commentary condemns.

sentences.zh: 石圖發于非常之文，此不從革之異也。

translations.literal: Stone diagrams appearing from extraordinary script are anomalies of disobedient metal.
translations.idiomatic: Cryptic stonework signals metal run wild.

sentences.zh: 晉定大業，多斃曹氏，石瑞文「大討曹」之應也。

translations.literal: Jin fulfilled its great enterprise by destroying much of the Cao clan—the stones' 'punish Cao' text matched that destiny.
translations.idiomatic: The inscription's vow to 'punish Cao' foretold Jin's triumph.

sentences.zh: 案劉歆以《春秋》石言于晉，為金石同類也，是為金不從革，失其性也，劉向以為石白色為主，屬白祥。

translations.literal: Liu Xin treated Spring and Autumn stones speaking in Jin as kin to metal and stone—metal refusing transformation; Liu Xiang read pale stone as sovereign portent, a white anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin classed speaking stone with rebellious metal; Liu Xiang added the white-omen reading.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝青龍中，盛修宮室，西取長安金狄，承露槃折，聲聞數十里，金狄泣，於是因留霸城。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Ming's Qinglong era: massive palace works; western crews dragged Chang'an's bronze figures—dew basin snapped; clang heard dozens of li; statues wept—so they halted at Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Metal gods wept when Qinglong-era builders shattered the Chang'an bronzes—an ill omen halted at Ba.

sentences.zh: 此金失其性而為異也。

translations.literal: This was metal losing nature and turning prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: Metal had plainly forsaken its virtue.

sentences.zh: 吳時，曆陽縣有岩穿，似印，咸云「石印封發，天下太平」。

translations.literal: Wu times: Liyang county bore a pierced rock like a seal—crowds chanted "when the stone seal opens, All-under-Heaven is at peace."
translations.idiomatic: A seal-shaped cavity at Liyang fed rumors of Wu's destined peace.

sentences.zh: 孫皓，印發。

translations.literal: Sun Hao's reign: the seal opened.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao saw the 'seal' crack open.

sentences.zh: 又，陽羨山有石穴，長十餘丈。

translations.literal: Also Yangxian mountain held a stone tunnel over ten zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxian also revealed a ten-zhang cavern.

sentences.zh: 皓初修武昌宮，有遷都之意。

translations.literal: Hao first refurbished Wuchang palace—harboring plans to move the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao rebuilt Wuchang as prelude to shifting the seat of power.

sentences.zh: 是時武昌為離宮。

translations.literal: Then Wuchang served as a detached palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang stood as a secondary court.

sentences.zh: 班固云「離宮與城郭同占」，飾城郭之謂也。

translations.literal: Ban Gu wrote that "detached palaces share omens with city walls"—meaning adorning ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu equated detached palaces with glorified battlements.

sentences.zh: 其後，皓出東關，遣丁奉至合肥，皓又大舉出華里，侵邊境之謂也。

translations.literal: Later Hao marched East Pass, sent Ding Feng toward Hefei, and mounted another grand drive at Huali—the encroaching frontier the gloss warns against.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's eastern campaigns fulfilled the 'border raid' clause.

sentences.zh: 故令金失其性，卒面縛而吳亡。

translations.literal: Thus metal lost nature; he ended bound Captive-of-Wu and Wu fell.
translations.idiomatic: Metal's curse concluded with Sun Hao bound and Wu extinguished.

sentences.zh: 惠帝閏二月，殿前六鐘皆出涕，五刻止。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui, intercalary second month: six bells before the hall wept tears of moisture for five ke.
translations.idiomatic: Six court bells wept metal tears under Emperor Hui.

sentences.zh: 前年賈后殺楊太后于金墉城，而賈后為惡不止，故鐘出涕，猶傷之也。

translations.literal: The year before Empress Jia murdered Empress Dowager Yang at Jinyong yet kept sinning—bells wept as if mourning her.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's bronze mourned Yang's murder and Jia's ceaseless cruelty.

sentences.zh: ，成都伐長沙，每夜戈戟鋒有火光如懸燭。

translations.literal: When Chengdu campaigned against Changsha, each night spearheads glowed like hanging candles.
translations.idiomatic: Night assaults between Chengdu and Changsha lit spearheads like lamps.

sentences.zh: 此輕人命，好攻戰，金失其性而為光變也。

translations.literal: This slighted human life and glorified battle—metal losing nature as fiery gleam.
translations.idiomatic: Wanton war turned weapons into will-o'-wisp flames.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，兵猶火也，不戢將自焚。

translations.literal: Heaven seemed to say: arms are like fire—unchecked, they consume their wielder.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven echoed the adage that armies, like fire, devour undisciplined masters.

sentences.zh: 成都不悟，終以敗亡。

translations.literal: Chengdu did not heed it and fell to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chengdu ignored the lesson and perished.

sentences.zh: 懷帝，項縣有魏豫州刺史賈逵石碑，生金可采，此金不從革而為變也。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai: Xiang county held Wei Inspector Jia Kui's stele sprouting mineable gold—metal refusing transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Gold blooming on Jia Kui's tablet proved metal deranged.

sentences.zh: 五月，汲桑作亂，群寇飆起。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Ji Sang rebelled; bandit armies exploded across the north.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang's fifth-month rising unleashed wholesale banditry.

sentences.zh: 清河王覃為世子時，所佩金鈴忽生起如粟者，康王母疑不祥，毀棄之。

translations.literal: While Prince Qinghe Tan was heir his belt-bell grew millet-like knobs—Prince Kang's mother smashed it as ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Tan's coronet bell sprouted tumors his grandmother destroyed as accursed.

sentences.zh: 及後為惠帝太子，不終於位，卒為司馬越所殺。

translations.literal: Later named Crown Prince under Emperor Hui he never succeeded—Sima Yue slew him.
translations.idiomatic: Elevated heir yet cut down by Sima Yue.

sentences.zh: 湣帝，石言於平陽。

translations.literal: Emperor Min: stone spoke at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Stones reportedly spoke at Pingyang under Emperor Min.

sentences.zh: 是時帝蒙塵亦在平陽，故有非言之物而言，妖之大者。

translations.literal: The exile emperor sheltered there too—mute things gaining speech marks supreme prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: With the throne lost in Pingyang, speech from stone was nightmare augury.

sentences.zh: 俄而帝為逆胡所弑。

translations.literal: Soon barbarian rebels assassinated him.
translations.idiomatic: Alien soldiers murdered him shortly after.

sentences.zh: 元帝，甘卓將襲王敦，既而中止。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan: Gan Zhuo planned to strike Wang Dun—then canceled it.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo hesitated to move against Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 及還，家多變怪，照鏡不見其頭。

translations.literal: Returning home he suffered endless omens; mirrors showed no head.
translations.idiomatic: His house filled with signs—reflections lacked his head.

sentences.zh: 此金失其性而為妖也。

translations.literal: Metal had lost nature and turned uncanny.
translations.idiomatic: Metal prodigy stalked him.

sentences.zh: 尋為敦所襲，遂夷滅。

translations.literal: Soon Wang Dun attacked and annihilated him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun crushed him soon thereafter.

sentences.zh: 石季龍時，鄴城鳳陽門上金鳳皇二頭飛入漳河。

translations.literal: Under Shi Hu twin golden phoenixes atop Ye's Fengyang Gate flew into the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu watched gilt phoenixes plunge from Ye's gate into the Zhang.

sentences.zh: 海西太和中，會稽山陰縣起倉，鑿地得兩大船，滿中錢，錢皆輪文大形。

translations.literal: Duke of Haixi, Taihe era: digging Shanyin's granary uncovered two barges jammed with broad wheel-rim coins.
translations.idiomatic: Granary works at Shanyin unearthed treasure barges of cash.

sentences.zh: 時日向暮，鑿者馳以告官，官夜遣防守甚嚴。

translations.literal: Near dusk laborers raced to officials who guarded the site through the night.
translations.idiomatic: Dig crews alerted magistrates who sealed the find overnight.

sentences.zh: 至明旦，失錢所在，惟有船存。

translations.literal: By dawn the coins vanished—only hulls remained.
translations.idiomatic: Dawn revealed empty hulls.

sentences.zh: 視其狀，悉有錢處。

translations.literal: Their outlines still marked where coin had lain.
translations.idiomatic: Imprints outlined vanished treasure.

sentences.zh: 安帝義熙初，東陽太守殷仲文照鏡不見其頭，尋亦誅翦，占與甘卓同也。

translations.literal: Emperor An, early Yixi: Dongyang prefect Yin Zhongwen saw no head in his mirror—soon executed—same reading as Gan Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongwen's headless reflection prefaced his execution like Gan Zhuo's.

sentences.zh: 水

translations.literal: Water.
translations.idiomatic: Water — the northern phase.

sentences.zh: =《傳》曰：「簡宗廟，不禱祠，廢祭祀，逆天時，則水不潤下。」

translations.literal: =The Commentary says: "If one neglects ancestral temples, fails to pray and sacrifice, abandons offerings, and opposes Heaven's seasons—then water does not moisten downward."
translations.idiomatic: Neglected shrines, silent prayers, and defiance of the calendar dry water's virtue.

sentences.zh: 說曰：水，北方，終藏萬物者也。

translations.literal: Explanation says: Water is north; it harbors the myriad things in their winter hiding.
translations.idiomatic: Northwater seals all life in winter storage.

sentences.zh: 其於人道，命終而形藏，精神放越。

translations.literal: On human paths life ends and form hides while spirit flies away.
translations.idiomatic: Death hides the body while souls wander.

sentences.zh: 聖人為之宗廟，以收魂氣，春秋祭祀，以終孝道。

translations.literal: Sages founded ancestral temples to gather wandering breath; spring and autumn sacrifices fulfill filial duty.
translations.idiomatic: Temples bind wandering qi; seasonal offerings finish filial love.

sentences.zh: 王者即位，必郊祀天地，禱祈神祇，望秩山川，懷柔百神，亡不宗事。

translations.literal: Kings upon accession sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, pray to spirits, honor mountains and rivers in rank, soothe the hundred gods—none left unworshiped.
translations.idiomatic: Accession demands suburban rites to Heaven, Earth, and every ranked spirit.

sentences.zh: 慎其齋戒，致其嚴敬，是故鬼神歆饗，多獲福助。

translations.literal: Careful fasting and reverent awe win ghostly favor and abundant blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Strict vigil wins the ancestors' feast.

sentences.zh: 此聖王所以順事陰氣，和神人也。

translations.literal: Thus sage kings harmonize Yin qi and unite gods with men.
translations.idiomatic: Such kings align Yin forces with the invisible realm.

sentences.zh: 及至發號施令，亦奉天時。

translations.literal: Even issuing commands follows Heaven's seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts too obey the calendar.

sentences.zh: 十二月咸得其氣，則陰陽調而終始成。

translations.literal: When all twelve months receive their proper qi, Yin and Yang tune and the year completes.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly qi in balance spins the cycle whole.

sentences.zh: 如此，則水得其性矣。

translations.literal: Thus water obtains its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Then water flows as ordained.

sentences.zh: 若乃不敬鬼神，政令逆時，水失其性。

translations.literal: If spirits are slighted and edicts defy seasons—water loses nature.
translations.idiomatic: Irreverence and mad policy befoul water.

sentences.zh: 霧水暴出，百川逆溢，壞鄉邑，溺人民，及淫雨傷稼穡，是為水不潤下。

translations.literal: Sudden fog-waters burst forth; hundred streams reverse and overflow; ruin hamlets and drown people; persistent rains spoil grain—this is water refusing to sink and nourish.
translations.idiomatic: Flash floods, backward rivers, drowned towns, and sodden crops spell rebellious water.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「顓事者加，誅罰絕理，厥災水。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yi Commentary says: "When tyrants multiply executions beyond justice, the calamity is flood.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang lists judicial cruelty summoning inundation.

sentences.zh: 其水也，雨，殺人，以隕霜，大風天黃。

translations.literal: Its flood becomes rain that kills men, hail-like frost, yellow heavens and great wind.
translations.idiomatic: Such floods ride killing rains, yellow skies, and lethal gales.

sentences.zh: 饑而不損，茲謂泰，厥大水，水殺人。

translations.literal: Famine without relief—called complacency—great flood follows and drowns people.
translations.idiomatic: Ignored famine invites drowning surge.

sentences.zh: 避遏有德，茲謂狂，厥水，水流殺人也。

translations.literal: Blocking worthies—called madness—brings currents that slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Suppressing virtue unleashes murderous currents.

sentences.zh: 已水則地生蟲。

translations.literal: When flood subsides worms breed in the soil.
translations.idiomatic: Receding waters hatch vermin.

sentences.zh: 歸獄不解，茲謂追非，厥水寒，殺人。

translations.literal: Unresolved punishments—called chasing wrong—bring chill flood killing men.
translations.idiomatic: Unfinished justice freezes fatal tides.

sentences.zh: 追誅不解，茲謂不理，厥水五穀不收。

translations.literal: Relentless executions—called disorder—bring flood with no harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Endless slaughter yields floods without grain.

sentences.zh: 大敗不解，茲謂皆陰，厥水流入國邑，隕霜殺穀。

translations.literal: Great defeat unchecked—called universal Yin—brings flood into capitals and frost killing grain.
translations.idiomatic: Total Yin dominance pours water through cities and kills crops with frost.

sentences.zh: 」董仲舒曰：「交兵結仇，伏屍流血，百姓愁怨，陰氣盛，故大水也。」

translations.literal: " Dong Zhongshu said: 'When arms cross and enmity knots, corpses lie in blood, the hundred surnames grieve and resent, Yin qi flourishes—therefore great flood.'"
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu linked mutual slaughter and popular despair to Yin tides and inundation.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝六月，大雨霖，伊洛溢，至津陽城門，漂數千家，殺人。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Wen, sixth month: great prolonged rain; Yi and Luo overflowed to Jinyang city gate, drifting several thousand households, killing people.
translations.idiomatic: Summer rains on the Yi and Luo swamped Luoyang's Jinyang Gate, drowning thousands of homes.

sentences.zh: 初，帝即位，自鄴遷洛，營造宮室，而不起宗廟。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor ascended the throne, he moved from Ye to Luo, built palace chambers, but did not raise ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi moved the capital to Luoyang yet left the royal shrine unbuilt.

sentences.zh: 太祖神主猶在鄴，嘗於建始殿饗祭如家人禮，終黃初不復還鄴。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor's spirit tablet still lay in Ye; he once feasted and sacrificed in Jianshi Hall with family rites, and through Huangchu never returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The founder's tablet stayed in Ye while Cao Pi offered makeshift rites in Jianshi Hall—never restoring the old shrine.

sentences.zh: 又郊社神祇，未有定位。

translations.literal: Moreover suburban and soil altars lacked fixed stations.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth altars also stood unplaced.

sentences.zh: 此簡宗廟廢祭祀之罰也。

translations.literal: This was punishment for scanting the temple and abandoning sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's rebuke for neglected ancestors.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權夏，茶陵縣鴻水溢出，漂二百餘家。

translations.literal: Wu Sun Quan, summer: Hong waters at Chaling county overflowed, drifting over two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's summer saw the Chaling torrent wash away two hundred homes.

sentences.zh: 十三年秋，丹陽、故鄣等縣又鴻水溢出。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year autumn: Danyang, Guchang, and other counties again saw Hong water overflow.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn of the thirteenth year reflooded Danyang and Guchang.

sentences.zh: 案權稱帝三十年，竟不於建鄴創七廟。

translations.literal: Case: during thirty years as emperor Quan never founded seven shrines at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan reigned three decades without the canonical seven-ancestor temple in Jianye.

sentences.zh: 惟父堅一廟遠在長沙，而郊祀禮闕。

translations.literal: Only a single hall for his father Jian far off in Changsha, and suburban rites were missing.
translations.idiomatic: Only Sun Jian's distant Changsha chapel remained; the great suburban liturgy lapsed.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾初，群臣奏宜郊祀，又不許。

translations.literal: At the start of the Jiahe era ministers petitioned for suburban sacrifice—again he refused.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers' pleas for sacrifice met refusal in the Jiahe years.

sentences.zh: 末年雖一南郊，而北郊遂無聞焉。

translations.literal: In his final year although once sacrificing south of the city, the northern suburban rite has no record.
translations.idiomatic: One southern suburb marked his reign—never its northern pair.

sentences.zh: 吳楚之望亦不見秩，反祀羅陽妖神，以求福助。

translations.literal: Wu and Chu tutelary gods likewise lacked ranked offerings; instead they sacrificed to Luoyang's demon gods hunting blessings.
translations.idiomatic: He neglected regional gods while honoring dubious spirits for favors.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，權簡宗廟，不禱祠，廢祭祀，故示此罰，欲其感悟也。

translations.literal: Heaven seemed to say Quan scanted temples, avoided prayer, abandoned sacrifice—therefore showed this penalty wishing him to awaken.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven flagged Sun Quan's shrine neglect hoping he would repent.

sentences.zh: ，吳又有大風湧水之異。

translations.literal: Moreover Wu again had great wind and surging water anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Wu also suffered hurricanes and tidal catastrophes.

sentences.zh: 是冬，權南郊，宜是鑒咎徵乎！

translations.literal: That winter Quan sacrificed south of the city—was this reflecting on prior omens?
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps his belated southern suburb answered Heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 還而寢疾，明年四月薨。

translations.literal: Returning he took to bed; fourth month next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill on his return and died the next spring.

sentences.zh: 一曰，權時信納譖訴，雖陸遜勳重，子和儲貳，猶不得其終，與漢安帝聽讒免楊震、廢太子同事也。

translations.literal: One explanation: Quan trusted slander—even Lu Xun's great merit and Heir-apparent Sun He's standing did not save them, matching Han Andi's listening to lies that dismissed Yang Zhen and deposed the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Court gossip ruined Lu Xun and Crown Prince He—parallel to Han tragedies involving Yang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 且赤烏中無年不用兵，百姓愁怨。

translations.literal: Moreover almost every Chiwu year mobilized arms until commoners groaned.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwu-era wars bred ceaseless popular resentment.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，將軍馬茂等又圖逆。

translations.literal: Eighth year autumn: General Ma Mao and others plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn of the eighth year brought Ma Mao's plot.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝九月，淫雨，冀、兗、徐、豫四州水出，沒溺殺人，漂失財產。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Ming, ninth month: excessive rain; Ji, Yan, Xu, Yu four provinces flooded, drowning people and sweeping away wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Sheets of rain drowned four provinces under Emperor Ming of Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝自初即位，便淫奢極欲，多占幼女，或奪士妻，崇飾宮室，妨害農戰，觸情恣欲，至是彌甚，號令逆時，饑不損役。

translations.literal: From first accession he indulged extravagance, seized young girls, robbed officers' wives, gilded halls, harmed farming and warfare, followed every whim—by now worst yet—commands opposed seasons; famine yet labor never eased.
translations.idiomatic: His reign layered lust, corvée, and reckless policy on starving peasants.

sentences.zh: 此水不潤下之應也。

translations.literal: This matched water refusing to sink and nourish.
translations.idiomatic: Classic symptoms of rebellious water.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮夏，大水。

translations.literal: Wu Sun Liang, summer: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang's summer brought inundation.

sentences.zh: 亮即位四年，乃立權廟。

translations.literal: Four years after Liang's accession he finally founded Quan's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Only after four years did Sun Liang dedicate Sun Quan's shrine.

sentences.zh: 又終吳世不上祖宗之號，不修嚴父之禮，昭穆之數有闕。

translations.literal: Through Wu's end they never honored founding ancestors by canonical titles nor observed stern-father rites—the Zhao-Mu sequence lacked.
translations.idiomatic: Wu ended without proper temple tablets or Zhao-Mu ordering.

sentences.zh: 亮及休、皓又並廢二郊，不秩群神。

translations.literal: Liang, Xiu, and Hao together abolished both suburban altars and ranked gods.
translations.idiomatic: Three sovereigns junked twin suburbs and neglected the pantheon.

sentences.zh: 此簡宗廟不祭祀之罰也。

translations.literal: This was punishment for scanting temples and ending sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Another heaven-sent penalty for forgotten ancestors.

sentences.zh: 又，是時孫峻專政，陰勝陽之應乎！

translations.literal: Moreover Sun Jun monopolized government—a response of Yin conquering Yang?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun's dictatorship embodied Yin ascendant.

sentences.zh: 孫休五月，大雨，水泉湧溢。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu, fifth month: great rain; springs surged and overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu's fifth month saw rains explode springs across Wu.

sentences.zh: 昔歲作浦裏塘，功費無數，而田不可成，士卒死叛，或自賊殺，百姓愁怨，陰氣盛也。

translations.literal: Prior year they built the Puli embankment—countless cost yet fields never formed; soldiers died or deserted or slew themselves; commoners groaned—Yin flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The ruinous Puli project wasted treasure, soldiers, and morale—pure Yin.

sentences.zh: 休又專任張布，退盛沖等，吳人賊之應也。

translations.literal: Xiu also wholly trusted Zhang Bu, cashiered Sheng Chong and others—Wu folk murdered him as consequence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bu's monopoly after Sheng Chong's exile invited assassination.

sentences.zh: 五年八月壬午，大雨震電，水泉湧溢。

translations.literal: Fifth year eighth month day renwu: great rain, thunder and lightning, springs surged.
translations.idiomatic: Renwu day brought thunderstorms and boiling groundwater.

sentences.zh: 武帝九月，青、徐、兗、豫四州大水。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, ninth month: Qing, Xu, Yan, Yu four provinces great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Western Jin's Emperor Wu watched four eastern provinces drown.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，大雨霖，河、洛、伊、沁皆溢，殺二百餘人。

translations.literal: Seventh year sixth month: prolonged rain; Yellow River, Luo, Yi, Qin all overflowed, killing over two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Month-long rain burst the Yellow River and tributaries with hundreds dead.

sentences.zh: 自帝即尊位，不加三后祖宗之號。

translations.literal: Since accession he added no canonical titles for three empresses or Founders.
translations.idiomatic: He withheld temple honors from mothers and dynastic founders.

sentences.zh: 又除明堂南郊五帝座，同稱昊天上帝，一位而已。

translations.literal: He removed Bright Hall's southern suburb seats for Five Emperors—calling all merely Supreme Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He collapsed five gods into one ambiguous Heaven.

sentences.zh: 又省先-{后}-配地之祀。

translations.literal: He also cut Former Empress joint sacrifices to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: He canceled earth-paired rites for the late empress.

sentences.zh: 此簡宗廟廢祭祀之罰也。

translations.literal: This was punishment for scanting temples and abandoning sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Temple neglect drew predictable floods.

sentences.zh: 咸甯元年九月，徐州大水。

translations.literal: Xianning first year ninth month: Xuzhou great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou flooded in Xianning's first autumn.

sentences.zh: 二年七月癸亥，河南、魏郡暴水，殺百餘人。

translations.literal: Second year seventh month day guihai: Henan and Wei commandery cloudburst killed over a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: A cloudburst drowned Henan and Wei.

sentences.zh: 閏月，荊州郡國五大水，流四千餘家。

translations.literal: Intercalary month: Jing province and kingdoms—five great floods, drifting four thousand-plus households.
translations.idiomatic: Five Jing-region floods displaced four thousand families.

sentences.zh: 去年采擇良家子女，露面入殿，帝親簡閱，務在姿色，不訪德行，有蔽匿者以不敬論，搢紳愁怨，天下非之，陰盛之應也。

translations.literal: Prior year they levied gentlewomen who entered the hall unveiled while the emperor personally screened them for beauty alone, ignoring virtue; concealment earned 'disrespect' charges—gentry groaned and All-under-Heaven condemned it—Yin ascendant.
translations.idiomatic: Palace beauty hunts humiliated families—ominous Yin.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，益、梁二州郡國八暴水，殺三百餘人。

translations.literal: Third year sixth month: Yi and Liang eight commanderies cloudburst killed over three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Yi-Liang districts drowned three hundred souls.

sentences.zh: 七月，荊州大水。

translations.literal: Seventh month: Jingzhou great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou flooded that summer.

sentences.zh: 九月，始平郡大水。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Shiping commandery great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Shiping county vanished under rain.

sentences.zh: 十月，青、徐、兗、豫、荊、益、梁七州又大水。

translations.literal: Tenth month: Qing, Xu, Yan, Yu, Jing, Yi, Liang seven provinces flooded again.
translations.idiomatic: Seven provinces reeled under repeated inundation.

sentences.zh: 是時賈充等用事專恣，而正人疏外者多，陰氣盛也。

translations.literal: Then Jia Chong and allies ran riot while upright men languished outside—Yin flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong's clique dominated while moral ministers sat idle.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，司、冀、兗、豫、荊、揚郡國二十大水，傷秋稼，壞屋室，有死者。

translations.literal: Fourth year seventh month: Si, Ji, Yan, Yu, Jing, Yang—twenty commanderies flooded, spoiling autumn crops, wrecking houses, with dead.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty commanderies lost harvest and housing to summer storms.

sentences.zh: 六月，泰山、江夏大水，泰山流三百家，殺六十餘人，江夏亦殺人。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Taishan and Jiangxia floods—Taishan swept three hundred households killing sixty-plus; Jiangxia also killed people.
translations.idiomatic: Taishan and Jiangxia torrents killed dozens.

sentences.zh: 時平吳後，王浚為元功而詆劾妄加，荀、賈為無謀而並蒙重賞，收吳姬五千，納之後宮，此其應也。

translations.literal: After Wu's conquest Wang Jun merited first rank yet suffered slander; Xun and Jia proved witless yet won lavish rewards; five thousand Wu women filled the harem—such deeds matched the omens.
translations.idiomatic: Post-conquest injustice and plunder mirrored Heaven's anger.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，兗州大水。

translations.literal: Fourth year seventh month: Yanzhou great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou drowned again.

sentences.zh: 十二月，河南及荊、揚六州大水。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Henan plus six Jing-Yang provinces flooded.
translations.idiomatic: Winter floods swept Henan and six southern provinces.

sentences.zh: 五年九月，郡國四大水，又隕霜。

translations.literal: Fifth year ninth month: four commanderies great flood with hail frost.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn brought flood and killing frost together.

sentences.zh: 是月，南安等五郡大水。

translations.literal: That month: Nan'an and four other commanderies flooded.
translations.idiomatic: Nan'an pentad vanished under rain.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，郡國十大水，壞廬舍。

translations.literal: Sixth year fourth month: ten commanderies flooded, wrecking cottages.
translations.idiomatic: Ten districts lost homes to spring surge.

sentences.zh: 七年九月，郡國八大水。

translations.literal: Seventh year ninth month: eight commanderies flooded.
translations.idiomatic: Eight commanderies flooded late summer.

sentences.zh: 八月六月，郡國八大水。

translations.literal: Eighth month and sixth month: eight commanderies flooded.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated summer and autumn waves struck eight commanderies.

sentences.zh: 惠帝，有水災。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui: flood disasters occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui's reign opened with inundations.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，潁川、淮南大水。

translations.literal: Fifth year fifth month: Yingchuan and Huainan great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan and Huainan drowned in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 六月，城陽、東莞大水，殺人，荊、揚、徐、兗、豫五州又水。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Chengyang and Dongguan floods killed people; Jing, Yang, Xu, Yan, Yu five provinces flooded again.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong seasides drowned while five heartland provinces sank.

sentences.zh: 是時帝即位已五載，猶未郊祀，其蒸嘗亦多不親行事。

translations.literal: By then five years on the throne he still performed no suburban sacrifice; seasonal offerings rarely saw his presence.
translations.idiomatic: Five years without suburb rites or personal ancestral meals.

sentences.zh: 此簡宗廟廢祭祀之罰。

translations.literal: This was punishment for scanting temples and abandoning sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Ignored shrines summoned more water.

sentences.zh: 六年五月，刑、揚二州大水。

translations.literal: Sixth year fifth month: Jing and Yang two provinces great flood.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing and Yang heartlands flooded together.

sentences.zh: 是時賈后亂朝，寵樹賈、郭，女主專政，陰氣盛之應也。

translations.literal: Then Empress Jia wrecked court, elevating Jia and Guo kin—female lord monopolized government—Yin ascendant.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia's matriarchy spelled Yin flooding.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，金墉城井溢。

translations.literal: Eighth year fifth month: Jinyong Citadel wells boiled over.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyong's wells erupted.

sentences.zh: 《漢志》，成帝時有此妖，後王莽僭逆。

translations.literal: Han Treatise records Cheng-era anomaly foreshadowing Wang Mang's usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Han history tied boiling wells to Wang Mang.

sentences.zh: 今有此妖，趙王倫篡位，倫廢帝於此城，井溢所在，其天意也。

translations.literal: Now the sign returned—Prince Zhao Lun seized throne after deposing the emperor here—well overflow matched Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun's coup at Jinyong replayed the Han omen.

sentences.zh: 九月，荊、揚、徐、冀、豫五州大水。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Jing, Yang, Xu, Ji, Yu five provinces great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Five provinces drowned that autumn.

sentences.zh: 是時賈后暴戾滋甚，韓謐驕猜彌扇，卒害太子，旋以禍滅。

translations.literal: Empress Jia turned brutal; Han Mi's arrogance peaked—soon they murdered the heir and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Nanfeng and Han Mi killed the crown prince then fell.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，宮中井水沸溢。

translations.literal: Ninth year fourth month: palace well water boiled over.
translations.idiomatic: Palace wells seethed.

sentences.zh: 永甯元年七月，南陽、東海大水。

translations.literal: Yongning first year seventh month: Nanyang and Donghai great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning opened with eastern floods.

sentences.zh: 是時齊王冏專政，陰盛之應也。

translations.literal: Then Prince Qi Sima Jiong monopolized government—Yin ascendant.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong's dictatorship meant Yin tide.

sentences.zh: 七月，兗、豫、徐、冀四州水。

translations.literal: Seventh month: Yan, Yu, Xu, Ji four provinces flooded.
translations.idiomatic: Four northern provinces drowned midsummer.

sentences.zh: 時將相力政，無尊主心，陰盛故也。

translations.literal: Generals and ministers wrestled power without honoring the sovereign—Yin ascendant.
translations.idiomatic: Warlord politics unmanned the throne—classic Yin.

sentences.zh: 孝懷帝四月，江東大水。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohuai, fourth month: east of the Yangtze great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangdong sank under spring rains.

sentences.zh: 時王導等潛懷翼戴之計，陰氣盛也。

translations.literal: Then Wang Dao secretly nurtured enthronement plots—Yin flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao's backstage maneuvering embodied Yin.

sentences.zh: 元帝六月，大水。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, sixth month: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan's summer washed Jinling.

sentences.zh: 是時王敦內懷不臣，傲很陵上，此陰氣盛也。

translations.literal: Then Wang Dun nursed treason, arrogant and encroaching—this Yin ascendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's rebellion typified surging Yin.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，又大水。

translations.literal: Fourth year seventh month: again great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Another midsummer inundation.

sentences.zh: 五月，荊州及丹陽、宣城、吳興、壽春大水。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Jingzhou plus Danyang, Xuancheng, Wuxing, Shouchun great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Heartland counties drowned early summer.

sentences.zh: 明帝五月，丹陽、宣城、吳興、壽春大水。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, fifth month: Danyang, Xuancheng, Wuxing, Shouchun great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming watched the same belt flood.

sentences.zh: 是時王敦威權震主，陰氣盛故也。

translations.literal: Then Wang Dun's might stunned the ruler—Yin ascendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's terror matched Yin water.

sentences.zh: 成帝五月，大水。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng, fifth month: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Young Cheng's reign flooded.

sentences.zh: 是時嗣主幼沖，母后稱制，庾亮以元舅決事禁中，陰勝陽故也。

translations.literal: Then the heir was infant, mother regent, Yu Liang as maternal uncle decided affairs inside the palace—Yin overcame Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Child emperor and Yu Liang's harem rule inverted Yin and Yang.

sentences.zh: 二年五月戊子，京都大水。

translations.literal: Second year fifth month day wuzi: capital great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang drowned on wuzi.

sentences.zh: 是冬，以蘇峻稱兵，都邑塗地。

translations.literal: That winter Su Jun raised arms and reduced the capital to mud.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun turned the capital into a slaughterfield.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，丹陽、宣城、吳興、會稽大水。

translations.literal: Fourth year seventh month: Danyang, Xuancheng, Wuxing, Kuaiji great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Lower Yangtze counties flooded again.

sentences.zh: 是冬，郭默作亂，荊豫共討之，半歲乃定，兵役之應也。

translations.literal: That winter Guo Mo rebelled; Jing and Yu jointly campaigned half a year to pacify—response of military labor.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo's mutiny answered flood with war.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，大水。

translations.literal: Seventh year fifth month: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Another fifth-month surge.

sentences.zh: 是時帝未親機務，政在大臣，陰勝陽也。

translations.literal: Then the emperor still did not personally handle policy—power lay with great ministers—Yin overcame Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Absent sovereigns ceded authority—Yin tide.

sentences.zh: 八月，長沙、武陵大水。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Changsha and Wuling great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan drowned late summer.

sentences.zh: 穆帝五月，大水。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu, fifth month: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu's boy reign flooded.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，大水。

translations.literal: Fifth year fifth month: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth year repeated inundation.

sentences.zh: 六年五月，又大水。

translations.literal: Sixth year fifth month: again great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Yet another fifth-month flood.

sentences.zh: 時幼主沖弱，母后臨朝，又將相大臣各執權政，與咸和初同事也。

translations.literal: Then the young lord was weak, mother listened behind screen, generals each seized authority—same pattern as Xianhe early years.
translations.idiomatic: Regency gridlock mirrored earlier crises.

sentences.zh: 七年七月甲辰夜，濤水入石頭，死者數百人。

translations.literal: Seventh year seventh month day jiachen night: tidal bore poured into Stone City killing hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: A night bore smashed Jinling's Stone fortress.

sentences.zh: 是時殷浩以私忿廢蔡謨，遐邇非之。

translations.literal: Then Yin Hao cashiered Cai Mo from private spite—all near and far condemned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao's feud with Cai Mo drew universal blame.

sentences.zh: 又幼主在上而殷桓交惡，選徒聚甲，各崇私權，陰勝陽之應也。

translations.literal: Moreover the young lord sat throne while Yin and Huan turned hostile, raising troops and armor, each exalting private power—response of Yin overcoming Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Child emperor amid Yin Hao–Huan Wen feud meant private armies and Yin flood.

sentences.zh: 一說，濤水入石頭，以為兵占。

translations.literal: One explanation: tidal bore entering Stone City prognosticates arms.
translations.idiomatic: Some read the Stone City bore purely as war omen.

sentences.zh: 是後殷浩、桓溫、謝尚、荀羨連年征伐，百姓愁怨也。

translations.literal: Afterward Yin Hao, Huan Wen, Xie Shang, and Xun Xian campaigned year after year—the hundred clans groaned.
translations.idiomatic: Endless eastern Jin expeditions left the people resentful.

sentences.zh: 五月，大水。

translations.literal: Fifth month: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: May brought another inundation.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，又大水。

translations.literal: Fifth year fourth month: again great flood.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth year's fourth month flooded again.

sentences.zh: 是時桓溫權制朝廷，專征伐，陰勝陽也。

translations.literal: Then Huan Wen controlled court authority and monopolized expeditions—Yin overcame Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's military dictatorship tipped Yin over Yang.

sentences.zh: 海西六月，京師大水，平地數尺，浸及太廟。

translations.literal: Duke of Haixi, sixth month: capital flood several chi deep on level ground—reached Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Summer floodwaters lapped the imperial shrine.

sentences.zh: 硃雀大航纜斷，三艘流入大江。

translations.literal: Zhuque Great Bridge cables snapped; three hulls drifted into the Great River.
translations.idiomatic: The capital pontoon broke adrift into the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 丹陽、晉陵、吳郡、吳興、臨海五郡又大水，稻稼蕩沒，黎庶饑饉。

translations.literal: Danyang, Jinling, Wu, Wuxing, and Linhai five commanderies flooded again—rice washed away, folk starving.
translations.idiomatic: The lower Yangtze rice bowl drowned and famine followed.

sentences.zh: 初，四年桓溫北伐敗績，十喪其九，五年又征淮南，逾歲乃克，百姓愁怨之應也。

translations.literal: At first in the fourth year Huan Wen's northern drive lost nine men of ten; the fifth year he struck Huainan and needed over a year to win—this answered popular resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Failed northern wars matched public bitterness.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝十二月壬午，濤水入石頭。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen, twelfth month day renwu: tidal bore entered Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: A bore swept Jinling's fortress zone.

sentences.zh: 明年，妖賊盧竦率其屬數百人入殿，略取武庫三庫甲仗，遊擊將軍毛安之討滅之，兵興、陰盛之應也。

translations.literal: Next year the sorcerer Lu Song led hundreds into the palace, looted three armories—General Mao Anzhi crushed them—omens of rising arms and flourishing Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Song's raid on Luoyang arsenals reflected Yin militarism.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝六月，大水。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, sixth month: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu's summer flood.

sentences.zh: 是時帝幼弱，政在將相。

translations.literal: Then the emperor was young and weak—policy rested with generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Child emperor; ministers held real power.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，大水。

translations.literal: Fifth year fifth month: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Another fifth-month surge.

sentences.zh: 六年六月，揚、荊、江三州大水。

translations.literal: Sixth year sixth month: Yang, Jing, and Jiang three provinces great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Three great river provinces drowned.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，始興、南康、廬陵大水，平地五丈。

translations.literal: Eighth year third month: Shixing, Nankang, and Luling floods five zhang deep on flat ground.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Jiangxi sank under fifteen-meter floods.

sentences.zh: 十年五月，大水。

translations.literal: Tenth year fifth month: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth year's May inundation.

sentences.zh: 自八年破苻堅後，有事中州，役無寧歲，愁怨之應也。

translations.literal: From the eighth year after defeating Fu Jian, campaigns in the Central Plains never rested—a response of grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Endless Huai River wars bred popular exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 十三年十二月，濤水入石頭，毀大航，殺人。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year twelfth month: bore entered Stone City, wrecked great bridge, killed people.
translations.idiomatic: Winter bore smashed the capital bridge.

sentences.zh: 明年，慕容氏寇擾司兗，鎮戍西北，疲於奔命，愁怨之應也。

translations.literal: Next year Murong raiders harassed Si and Yan—garrisons on the northwest collapsed from exhaustion—a grievance response.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier fatigue mirrored flood omens.

sentences.zh: 十五年七月，沔中諸郡及兗州大水。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year seventh month: Han River commanderies and Yanzhou great flood.
translations.idiomatic: The Han basin and Yanzhou drowned.

sentences.zh: 是時緣河紛爭，征戍勤瘁之應也。

translations.literal: Then Yellow River theaters quarreled endlessly—a response of weary conscripts.
translations.idiomatic: Riverine warfare drained the armies.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月甲寅，濤水入石頭，毀大航，漂船舫，有死者。

translations.literal: Seventh year seventeenth cycle sixth month day jiayin: bore entered Stone City, ruined great bridge, swept barges—with dead.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayin bore shattered shipping at Stone City.

sentences.zh: 京口西浦亦濤入殺人。

translations.literal: Jingkou west inlet also saw bore intrude killing people.
translations.idiomatic: Jingkou's harbor drowned souls too.

sentences.zh: 永嘉郡潮水湧起，近海四縣人多死。

translations.literal: Yongjia commandery tides surged—four coastal counties lost many lives.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang's tidal bore killed thousands.

sentences.zh: 後四年帝崩，而王恭再攻京師，京師亦發眾以禦之，兵彼頻興，百姓愁怨之應也。

translations.literal: Four years later the emperor died; Wang Gong twice attacked the capital while the capital mobilized to resist—arms arose repeatedly—a grievance response.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous chaos echoed the floods.

sentences.zh: 十八年六月己亥，始興、南康、廬陵大水，深五丈。

translations.literal: Eighteenth year sixth month day jihai: Shixing, Nankang, and Luling flooded five zhang deep.
translations.idiomatic: Another fifteen-meter flood hit southern commanderies.

sentences.zh: 十九年七月，荊徐大水，傷秋稼。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year seventh month: Jing and Xu great flood, spoiling autumn crops.
translations.idiomatic: Jing-Xu autumn harvest ruined.

sentences.zh: 二十年六月，荊徐又大水。

translations.literal: Twentieth year sixth month: Jing and Xu flooded again.
translations.idiomatic: The pair flooded anew next summer.

sentences.zh: 二十一年五月癸卯，大水。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year fifth month day guimao: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Guimao day brought universal inundation.

sentences.zh: 是時政事多弊，兆庶非之。

translations.literal: Then government affairs were mostly corrupt—myriad commoners condemned them.
translations.idiomatic: Rotten policy drew popular curses.

sentences.zh: 安帝五月，荊州大水，平地三丈。

translations.literal: Emperor An, fifth month: Jingzhou flood three zhang deep on flat ground.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou sank three zhang.

sentences.zh: 去年殷仲堪舉兵向京師，是年春又殺郗恢，陰盛作威之應也。

translations.literal: Prior year Yin Zhongkan marched on the capital; this spring he killed Xi Hui—a response of Yin wielding terror.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan's violence epitomized Yin ascendant.

sentences.zh: 仲堪尋亦敗亡。

translations.literal: Zhongkan soon fell and perished.
translations.idiomatic: He died in defeat.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，大水。

translations.literal: Fifth year fifth month: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Another spring flood.

sentences.zh: 是時會稽王世子元顯作威陵上，又桓玄擅西夏，孫恩亂東國，陰勝陽之應也。

translations.literal: Then Prince Kuaiji's heir Yuanxian lorded over the throne; Huan Xuan dominated the west; Sun En ravaged the east—Yin overcame Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian, Huan Xuan, and Sun En split the realm—pure Yin.

sentences.zh: 十二月，桓玄篡位。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Huan Xuan usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan seized the yellow robe.

sentences.zh: 其明年二月庚寅夜，濤水入石頭。

translations.literal: Next year second month day gengyin night: bore entered Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyin night bore returned.

sentences.zh: 商旅方舟萬計，漂敗流斷，骸胔相望。

translations.literal: Merchant convoys counted in myriad hulls—smashed, adrift, corpses bobbing everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Trade fleets shattered along the stone shore.

sentences.zh: 江左雖頻有濤變，未有若斯之甚。

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze often saw bores—never this severe.
translations.idiomatic: No Jin bore matched that slaughter.

sentences.zh: 三月，義軍克京都，玄敗走，遂夷滅之。

translations.literal: Third month: righteous army took capital—Xuan fled defeated and was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's host crushed Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 三年二月己丑朔夜，濤水入石頭，漂沒殺人，大航流敗。

translations.literal: Third year second month day jichou new-moon night: bore entered Stone City, drowned and killed, great bridge wrecked.
translations.idiomatic: Jichou-night bore ruined the bridge again.

sentences.zh: 十二月己未，濤水入石頭。

translations.literal: Twelfth month day jiwei: bore entered Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Jiwei bore struck Stone City.

sentences.zh: 二年十二月己未夜，濤水入石頭。

translations.literal: Second year twelfth month jiwei night: bore entered Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Another jiwei-night surge.

sentences.zh: 明年，駱球父環潛結桓胤、殷仲文等謀作亂，劉稚亦謀反，凡所誅滅數十家。

translations.literal: Next year Luo Qiu's father Huan secretly linked Huan Yin, Yin Zhongwen plotting revolt—Liu Zhi also rebelled—dozens of clans extirpated.
translations.idiomatic: Plotters died by the score after the omens.

sentences.zh: 三年五月丙午，大水。

translations.literal: Third year fifth month day bingwu: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwu flood.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月戊寅，濤水入石頭。

translations.literal: Fourth year twelfth month day wuyin: bore entered Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyin bore.

sentences.zh: 明年，王旅北討。

translations.literal: Next year royal army campaigned north.
translations.idiomatic: Northern expedition followed.

sentences.zh: 六年五月丁巳，大水。

translations.literal: Sixth year fifth month day dingsi: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Dingsi deluge.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，盧循至蔡洲。

translations.literal: Day yichou: the rebel Lu Xun reached Cai Isle.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun's warfleet closed on Cai Isle.

sentences.zh: 八年六月，大水。

translations.literal: Eighth year sixth month: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth-year summer flood.

sentences.zh: 九年五月辛巳，大水。

translations.literal: Ninth year fifth month day xinsi: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Xinsi inundation.

sentences.zh: 十年五月丁丑，大水。

translations.literal: Tenth year fifth month day dingchou: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Dingchou flood.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，西明門地穿，湧水出，毀門扇及限，亦水沴土也。

translations.literal: Day wuyin: Ximing Gate earth split—water gushed, ruined doors and sills—also water encroaching on earth.
translations.idiomatic: West gate sinkhole vomited water—water harming earth.

sentences.zh: 七月乙丑，淮北風災，大水殺人。

translations.literal: Seventh month day yichou: Huai north wind disaster—great flood killed people.
translations.idiomatic: Huai winds and floods killed.

sentences.zh: 十一年七月丙戌，大水，淹漬太廟，百官赴救。

translations.literal: Eleventh year seventh month day bingxu: great flood, soaked Grand Temple—hundred officials rushed to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Flood threatened the ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 明年，王旅北討關河。

translations.literal: Next year royal army campaigned north toward Guan and He.
translations.idiomatic: Northern drive toward the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 敬用五事

translations.literal: Earnestly Employ the Five Matters
translations.idiomatic: Section: The Five Governance Countenances.

sentences.zh: 《經》曰：「敬用五事：一曰貌，二曰言，三曰視，四曰聽，五曰思。

translations.literal: The Classic says: "Earnestly employ the five matters: first countenance, second speech, third sight, fourth hearing, fifth thought."
translations.idiomatic: The canon lists the five royal virtues of deportment, word, vision, audience, and reflection.

sentences.zh: 貌曰恭，言曰從，視曰明，聽曰聰，思曰睿。

translations.literal: Countenance is called respectful; speech compliant; sight clear; hearing acute; thought discerning.
translations.idiomatic: Each faculty pairs with a moral quality.

sentences.zh: 恭作肅，從作乂，明作哲，聰作謀，睿作聖。

translations.literal: Respect becomes solemnity; compliance becomes order; clarity becomes wisdom; acuity becomes counsel; discernment becomes sageliness.
translations.idiomatic: Virtues compound into political gifts.

sentences.zh: 休徵：曰肅，時雨若；

translations.literal: Auspicious signs: solemnity brings timely rain;
translations.idiomatic: When awe rules, rains fall on time.

sentences.zh: 乂，時晹若；

translations.literal: order brings timely sunshine;
translations.idiomatic: Harmony opens clear skies.

sentences.zh: 哲，時燠若；

translations.literal: wisdom brings timely warmth;
translations.idiomatic: Insight warms the seasons.

sentences.zh: 謀，時寒若；

translations.literal: counsel brings timely cold;
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation tempers winter.

sentences.zh: 聖，時風若。

translations.literal: sageliness brings timely wind.
translations.idiomatic: Sagely rule breathes fair winds.

sentences.zh: 咎徵：曰狂，恆雨若；

translations.literal: Calamity signs: madness brings constant rain;
translations.idiomatic: Madness summons endless rain.

sentences.zh: 僭，恆晹若；

translations.literal: presumption brings constant glare;
translations.idiomatic: Arrogance bakes the fields.

sentences.zh: 豫，恆燠若；

translations.literal: ease brings constant heat;
translations.idiomatic: Complacency smothers with heat.

sentences.zh: 急，恆寒若；

translations.literal: haste brings constant cold;
translations.idiomatic: Rashness freezes the year.

sentences.zh: {雨瞀}，恆風若。」

translations.literal: mist and blur bring constant wind."
translations.idiomatic: Obscured vision pairs with endless wind.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「貌之不恭，是謂不肅，厥咎狂，厥罰恆雨，厥極惡。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "When deportment lacks respect, called lacking solemnity, its fault is madness, its punishment constant rain, its extreme wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Disrespect triggers madness, flood, and moral collapse.

sentences.zh: 時則有服妖，時則有龜孽，時則有雞禍，時則有下體生上之痾，時則有青眚青祥。

translations.literal: Then appear costume prodigies, turtle calamities, chicken disasters, lower-body growing upper ailments, green misfortunes and green auguries.
translations.idiomatic: A litany of bizarre fauna and dress omens follows.

sentences.zh: 惟金沴木。」

translations.literal: Only metal encroaches on wood."
translations.idiomatic: Metal's qi harms wood.

sentences.zh: 說曰：凡草木之類謂之妖。

translations.literal: Explanation says: generally plants called 'prodigies.'
translations.idiomatic: Vegetation anomalies rank as yao.

sentences.zh: 妖猶夭胎，言尚微也。

translations.literal: Prodigy means still in embryo— barely manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Yao hints at incipient ill.

sentences.zh: 蟲豸之類謂之孽。

translations.literal: Creeping things called 'calamities.'
translations.idiomatic: Insects are nie.

sentences.zh: 孽則芽孽矣。

translations.literal: Calamity then sprouts like buds.
translations.idiomatic: Nie signals sprouting harm.

sentences.zh: 及六畜，謂之禍，言其著也。

translations.literal: Reaching domestic beasts called 'disaster'—manifest evil.
translations.idiomatic: Livestock omens are huo—open harm.

sentences.zh: 及人，謂之痾。

translations.literal: Reaching humans called 'ailment.'
translations.idiomatic: Human signs are e—personal sickness.

sentences.zh: 痾，病貌也，言浸深也。

translations.literal: Ailment is sickly deportment—deepening penetration.
translations.idiomatic: E describes worsening symptoms.

sentences.zh: 甚則有異物生，謂之眚；

translations.literal: Extreme cases spawn alien things called 'internal misfortune;'
translations.idiomatic: Severe cases yield inner sheng.

sentences.zh: 自外來，謂之祥。

translations.literal: coming from outside called 'augury.'
translations.idiomatic: Outward agents are xiang.

sentences.zh: 祥，猶禎也。

translations.literal: Augury parallels blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang resembles zhen.

sentences.zh: 氣相傷，謂之沴。

translations.literal: Qi harming qi called 'encroachment.'
translations.idiomatic: Mutual injury is li.

sentences.zh: 沴猶臨蒞，不和意也。

translations.literal: Encroachment means hostile looming—discord.
translations.idiomatic: Li implies malign friction.

sentences.zh: 每一事云「時則」以絕之，言非必俱至，或有或亡，或在前或在後。

translations.literal: Each matter adds 'then appears' to close—meaning not all arrive together; some exist, some vanish; some earlier, some later.
translations.idiomatic: The formula marks contingent omens.

sentences.zh: 孝武時，夏侯始昌通《五經》，善推《五行傳》，以傳族子夏侯勝，下及許商，皆以教所賢弟子。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xiaowu's reign Xiahou Shichang mastered the Five Classics and excelled at extending the Five Elements Commentary—he transmitted to nephew Xiahou Sheng down to Xu Shang—all teaching worthy disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Western Han masters chained the Hong Fan gloss across generations.

sentences.zh: 其傳與劉向同，惟劉歆傳獨異。

translations.literal: Their transmission matched Liu Xiang—only Liu Xin's version diverged.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin alone broke with Liu Xiang.

sentences.zh: 貌之不恭，是謂不肅。

translations.literal: Deportment lacking respect is called lacking solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss opens with irreverent bearing.

sentences.zh: 肅，敬也。

translations.literal: Solemnity means reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Su is awe.

sentences.zh: 內曰恭，外曰敬。

translations.literal: Inner is called respectful; outer called reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Gong within, jing without.

sentences.zh: 人君行己，體貌不恭，怠慢驕蹇，則不能敬萬事，失則狂易，故其咎狂也。

translations.literal: If the lord conducts himself with slovenly deportment, negligent pride, he cannot reverence the myriad tasks—failure turns manic—therefore the fault is madness.
translations.idiomatic: Royal laziness slides into mania.

sentences.zh: 上慢下暴，則陰氣勝，故其罰常雨也。

translations.literal: Superiors slack while inferiors rage—Yin qi prevails—therefore punishment is constant rain.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogance aloft draws endless Yin rain.

sentences.zh: 水傷百穀，衣食不足，則奸宄並作，故其極惡也。

translations.literal: Water harms grain—clothing and food fall short—then villainy rises together—therefore the extreme is wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Famine from flood breeds crime.

sentences.zh: 一曰，人多被刑，或形貌醜惡，亦是也。

translations.literal: One explanation: many people punished or grotesquely disfigured also counts.
translations.idiomatic: Mass mutilation mirrors the same fault.

sentences.zh: 風俗狂慢，變節易度，則為剽輕奇怪之服，故有服妖。

translations.literal: When customs turn manic and measures shift, people don bizarre light garments—hence costume prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: Fashion anomalies signal mad manners.

sentences.zh: 水類動，故有龜孽。

translations.literal: Water-kind creatures stir—hence turtle calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Turtle omens belong to moving Yin.

sentences.zh: 于《易》，《巽》為雞。

translations.literal: In the Changes Xun is chicken.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou yi maps Xun to fowl.

sentences.zh: 雞有冠、距，文武之貌。

translations.literal: Chickens bear comb and spur—the image of civil and martial deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Cocks symbolize regalia.

sentences.zh: 而不為威，貌氣毀，故有雞禍。

translations.literal: Yet they lack true awe—deportment qi ruined—hence chicken disasters.
translations.idiomatic: When ritual awe fails, fowl portents strike.

sentences.zh: 一曰，水歲多雞死及為怪，亦是也。

translations.literal: One explanation: years of water many chickens die or turn prodigious—also counts.
translations.idiomatic: Chicken die-offs in wet years belong to the same family of omens.

sentences.zh: 上失威儀，則有強臣害君上者，故有下體生於上之痾。

translations.literal: When superiors lose awe-inspiring deportment, powerful ministers harm the lord—therefore lower-body grows upon upper-body ailments.
translations.idiomatic: Collapsed dignity invites ministers who usurp the throne—literal body-upon-body prodigies.

sentences.zh: 木色青，故有青眚青祥。

translations.literal: Wood's color is green—therefore green misfortunes and green auguries.
translations.idiomatic: Wood-phase faults tint omens jade-green.

sentences.zh: 凡貌傷者病木氣，木氣病則金沴之，沖氣相通也。

translations.literal: Generally deportment injuries afflict wood qi; wood qi illness then metal encroaches—clashing qi interpenetrates.
translations.idiomatic: Demeanor faults harm wood; metal strikes wood in turn.

sentences.zh: 于《易》，《震》在東方，為春為木；

translations.literal: In the Changes Zhen lies east—as spring and wood.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen trigram maps east and spring wood.

sentences.zh: 《兌》在西方，為秋為金；

translations.literal: Dui lies west—as autumn and metal.
translations.idiomatic: Dui maps west and autumn metal.

sentences.zh: 《離》在南方，為夏為火；

translations.literal: Li lies south—as summer and fire.
translations.idiomatic: Li maps south and midsummer fire.

sentences.zh: 《坎》在北方，為冬為水。

translations.literal: Kan lies north—as winter and water.
translations.idiomatic: Kan maps north and winter water.

sentences.zh: 春與秋日夜分，寒暑平，是以金木之氣易以相變，故貌傷則致秋陰常雨，言傷則致春陽常旱也。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn divide day and night evenly; cold and heat balance—metal and wood qi therefore readily trade places—hence deportment injury brings autumn-like Yin constant rain; speech injury brings spring-like Yang constant drought.
translations.idiomatic: Balanced seasons let metal and wood swap energies—manners fault to flood; words fault to drought.

sentences.zh: 至於冬夏，日夜相反，寒暑殊絕，水火之氣不得相並，故視傷常燠、聽傷常寒者，其氣然也。

translations.literal: Winter and summer reverse day and night; cold and heat extremes never meet—water and fire cannot combine—therefore sight injury brings constant heat; hearing injury brings constant cold—qi behaves thus.
translations.idiomatic: Solstice extremes isolate fire and water—vision errs toward heat, hearing toward chill.

sentences.zh: 逆之，其極曰惡；

translations.literal: Opposing it, the extreme is called wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Defiance caps in villainy.

sentences.zh: 順之，其福曰攸好德。

translations.literal: Following it, the blessing is called cherishing virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Compliance crowns in love of virtue.

sentences.zh: 劉歆《貌傳》曰有鱗蟲之孽，羊禍，鼻痾。

translations.literal: Liu Xin's Deportment Gloss lists scale-creature calamities, sheep disasters, nose ailments.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin's schema piles animal and nasal omens.

sentences.zh: 說以為于天文東方辰為龍星，故為鱗蟲。

translations.literal: Explanation takes astronomy's east constellation chen as dragon stars—hence scale creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern asterisms become dragon-scale prodigies.

sentences.zh: 于《易》，《兌》為羊，木為金所病，故致羊禍，與常雨同應。

translations.literal: In the Changes Dui is sheep; wood afflicted by metal brings sheep disasters—matching constant rain.
translations.idiomatic: Dui-sheep symbolism ties wood-metal strife to ceaseless rain—or so one theory runs.

sentences.zh: 此說非是。

translations.literal: This explanation is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: The treatise rejects that pairing.

sentences.zh: 春與秋氣陰陽相敵，木病金盛，故能相並，惟此一事耳。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn Yin and Yang contend evenly—wood sick while metal strong—only then can they combine—unique case.
translations.idiomatic: Only equinox seasons balance wood illness with metal surge.

sentences.zh: 禍與妖痾祥眚同類，不得獨異。

translations.literal: Disasters align with prodigies, ailments, auguries, internal misfortune—same class—not uniquely different.
translations.idiomatic: All anomaly categories intergrade.

sentences.zh: 魏尚書鄧颺揚行步馳縱，筋不束體，坐起傾倚，若無手足，此貌之不恭也。

translations.literal: Wei Masters of Writing Deng Yang walked loose-limbed and reckless—sinews not binding body—sitting and rising tilted as without hands or feet—this was deportment lacking respect.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yang's twitching gait matched classic 'lack of solemnity.'

sentences.zh: 管輅謂之鬼躁。

translations.literal: Guan Lu called it ghost restlessness.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu dubbed his twitch ghost-frantic.

sentences.zh: 鬼躁者，凶終之徵，後卒誅也。

translations.literal: Ghost restlessness marks violent end—later indeed executed.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss foretold Deng Yang's execution.

sentences.zh: 惠帝元康中，貴遊子弟相與為散發倮身之飲，對弄婢妾，逆之者傷好，非之者負譏，希世之士恥不與焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui's Yuankang era noble youths wore loose hair and naked revels—dallying with maids—defiers harmed friendships—critics earned ridicule—fashionable men shunned abstention.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang elite staged hair-down orgies—classic deportment collapse.

sentences.zh: 蓋貌之不恭，胡狄侵中國之萌也。

translations.literal: Generally deportment lacking respect sprouts barbarian invasion of the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Such manners foreshadowed Five Hu upheaval.

sentences.zh: 其後遂有五胡之亂，此又失在狂也。

translations.literal: Afterward Five Hu chaos arose—another fault of madness.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian tide answered manic ritual.

sentences.zh: 元康中，賈謐親貴，數入二宮，與儲君遊戲，無降下心。

translations.literal: Yuankang era Jia Mi grew intimate and noble—often entered both palaces—played with heir-apparent—never humbled himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi treated the crown prince as playmate.

sentences.zh: 又嘗因弈棋爭道，成都王穎厲色曰：「皇太子國之儲貳，賈謐何敢無禮！

translations.literal: Once quarreling over weiqi lanes Prince Chengdu Sima Ying sternly said: 'The heir-apparent is state pillar—how dare Jia Mi lack propriety!'
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying rebuked Jia Mi at the chessboard.

sentences.zh: 」謐猶不悛，故及於禍，貌不恭之罰也。

translations.literal: " Mi still did not reform—therefore met disaster—punishment for deportment lacking respect.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi's arrogance earned ruin.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏既誅趙王倫，因留輔政，坐拜百官，符敕臺府，淫醟專驕，不一朝覲，此狂恣不肅之咎也。

translations.literal: Prince Qi Sima Jiong after executing Prince Zhao Lun stayed to assist government—sat conferring titles on hundred officials—writs commanded Secretariat—debauchery and arrogance—never once court-audienced—this was manic lack of solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong hijacked court ritual from his chair.

sentences.zh: 天下莫不高其功而慮其亡也，冏終弗改，遂致夷滅。

translations.literal: All-under-Heaven praised his merit yet feared his fall—Jiong never mended—thereupon annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: His swagger invited extinction.

sentences.zh: 司馬道子於府園內列肆，使姬人酤鬻，身自貿易。

sentences.zh: 許昌城南門無故自崩，帝心惡之，遂不入，還洛陽。

translations.literal: Xuchang south gate without cause collapsed—emperor loathed it—did not enter—returned Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gate ruin turned Cao Pi back.

sentences.zh: 此金沴木，木動之也。

translations.literal: This metal encroaching wood—wood stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Metal qi shattered timber gate.

sentences.zh: 五月，宮車晏駕。

translations.literal: Fifth month palace carriage ascended feast—emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi died that spring.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「上下咸悖，厥妖也城門壞。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang Yi Commentary says: 'Superiors and inferiors alike rebel—prodigy city gate ruins.'
translations.idiomatic: Mutual treason broke portals.

sentences.zh: 元帝六月，吳郡米廡無故自壞。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan sixth month: Wu commandery granary gallery without cause collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu granary fell spontaneously.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，夫米廡，貨糴之屋，無故自壞，此五穀踴貴，所以無糴賣也。

translations.literal: Heaven seemed to say granary is house for selling grain—without cause collapsing means five grains soar dear—hence nothing to sell.
translations.idiomatic: Empty granaries augured famine.

sentences.zh: 是歲遂大饑，死者千數焉。

translations.literal: That year great famine—dead counted in thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands starved.

sentences.zh: 明帝太甯元年，周莚自歸王敦，既立其宅宇，所起五間六梁，一時躍出墜地，餘桁猶亙柱頭。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming Taining first year Zhou Yan defected to Wang Dun—after raising his residence five bays six beams simultaneously leapt out fell ground—remaining rafters still bridged column heads.
translations.idiomatic: Roof beams ejected themselves.

sentences.zh: 此金沴木也。

translations.literal: This metal encroaching wood.
translations.idiomatic: Classic metal-wood clash.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，錢鳳謀亂，遂族滅莚，而湖熟尋亦為墟矣。

translations.literal: Next year fifth month Qian Feng plotted rebellion—thereupon clan-extinguished Yan—while Hushu soon wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yan died in Wang Dun purge.

sentences.zh: 安帝正月丙子，會稽王世子元顯將討桓玄，建牙竿于揚州南門，其東者難立，良久乃正。

translations.literal: Emperor An first month day bingzi: Prince Kuaiji heir Yuanxian about to campaign against Huan Xuan—raised mast at Yangzhou south gate—eastern pole resisted erecting—long time before straight.
translations.idiomatic: Army mast refused to stand upright.

sentences.zh: 近沴妖也。

translations.literal: Near encroachment prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: Marshaling omen of discord.

sentences.zh: 而元顯尋為玄所擒。

translations.literal: Yuanxian soon captured by Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian fell to Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，樂賢堂壞。

translations.literal: Third year fifth month Yuxian Hall ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Hall of Cherishing Worthies collapsed.

sentences.zh: 時帝嚚眊，無樂賢之心，故此堂是沴。

translations.literal: Then emperor dim-witted—lacked heart cherishing worthies—therefore hall encroached.
translations.idiomatic: Brain-dead throne despised talent.

sentences.zh: 五月，國子聖堂壞。

translations.literal: Fifth month Imperial Academy Sage Hall ruined.
translations.idiomatic: National university shrine fell.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，聖堂，禮樂之本，無故自壞，業祚將墜之象。

translations.literal: Heaven seemed to say Sage Hall is root of ritual music—without cause collapsing—image merit mandate about to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Ruined school augured abdication.

sentences.zh: 未及十年而禪位焉。

translations.literal: Before ten years passed abdicated throne.
translations.idiomatic: Song usurpation followed.
